### Ep.5: Oxford's Prof. John Todd on the Revolution Powering Precision Medicine
Prof. John Todd, Professor of Precision Medicine at the University of Oxford's Nuffield Department of Medicine, explains why enabling technologies — from PCR to today's proteomics platforms — drive scientific discovery, and why Alamar Bioscience's NULISA assay (including its Argo platform and CNS panel) has become central to his lab's work in type 1 diabetes, neuroinflammation, and biomarker-driven medicine.
![Ep. 4: Oxford's Prof. John Todd discusses NULISA for Type 1 Diabetes Research](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Episode4-prof.john_.png)
### Ep. 4: Oxford's Prof. John Todd discusses NULISA for Type 1 Diabetes Research
Prof. John Todd, Professor of Precision Medicine at the University of Oxford's Nuffield Department of Medicine, explains why his lab at the Centre for Human Genetics added Alamar Bioscience's NULISA assay and Argo platform to its proteomics toolkit — and what it revealed about interleukin-2 (IL-2) therapy in type 1 diabetes.
![Ep. 3: Dr. Cheryl Wellington on Fluid Biomarkers in Alzheimer’s, TBI, and Stroke](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Episode_3.jpg)
### Ep. 3: Dr. Cheryl Wellington on Fluid Biomarkers in Alzheimer’s, TBI, and Stroke
In this third episode of The Biomarker Edge, Dr. Cheryl Wellington from the University of British Columbia, discusses her work advancing fluid biomarkers in Alzheimer’s disease, traumatic brain injury, and stroke. She shares insights on launching a new biomarker core facility, building collaborations with over 120 clinical partners, and expanding biomarker applications from pediatric to geriatric care. Dr. Wellington highlights how ultra-sensitive, multiplexed technologies like ARGO™ and NULISA™ are enabling low-volume specimen analysis, broad biomarker panels, and translational research that bridges clinical and pre-clinical models.
![Ep. 2: Dr. Nicholas Ashton on Blood-Based Biomarkers in Alzheimer's Disease](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Episode_2.jpg)
### Ep. 2: Dr. Nicholas Ashton on Blood-Based Biomarkers in Alzheimer's Disease
In this episode of The Biomarker Edge series, Dr. Nicholas Ashton from Banner Health explores the clinical utility of emerging plasma biomarkers—including p-tau217, NfL, GFAP, and others—in Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias. He discusses how high-sensitivity, multiplex platforms like NULISA™ are enabling researchers to detect low-abundance CNS proteins in blood with greater precision than ever before.
![Ep 1: Dr. Henrik Zetterberg on Fluid Biomarkers in Neurodegenerative Disease](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Episode_1.jpg)
### Ep 1: Dr. Henrik Zetterberg on Fluid Biomarkers in Neurodegenerative Disease
In this premiere episode of The Biomarker Edge, world-renowned neurologist and biomarker expert Dr. Henrik Zetterberg discusses the urgent need for ultra-sensitive, multiplexed fluid biomarker assays to advance neurodegenerative disease research.

## Steve Williams, MD, PhD
CSO
Dr. Willams serves as the company’s Chief Scientific Officer. He was previously Chief Medical Officer at Standard Biotools and at SomaLogic where he pioneered the discipline for discovery and validation of predictive, diagnostic and prognostic models using machine-learning applied to large-plex proteomics. 20 such tests were used for drug characterization, safety and efficacy when incorporated in clinical drug trials at Pharma/Biotech and 17 different multivariate tests were validated and translated into regulated healthcare uses. Prior to SomaLogic, Dr. Williams was at Pfizer in the UK and the USA as a clinical triallist in Translational Medicine, and subsequently as VP, Global Clinical Technology. He sat on the National Advisory Council for the National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering, the Executive Committee for the FNIH Biomarkers Consortium, and worked with FDA and PhRMA on developing evidentiary standards for biomarker qualification. Dr. William’s medical training was in London, at Charing Cross and Westminster Medical School, followed by a PhD in medicine/physiology at the same institution and training in Radiology at the University of Newcastle Upon Tyne. Steve is co-inventor on 26 proteomics patents and author/coauthor on multiple foundational proteomics manuscripts.

## Justin McAnear
CFO
Mr. McAnear serves as the company’s Chief Financial Officer. He brings over 25 years of operational and financial leadership experience across various sectors and was instrumental in taking 10x Genomics public in 2019, serving as its CFO for over five years. Mr. McAnear served for over 3 years as Tesla’s VP of Worldwide Finance and Operations, supporting landmark initiatives such as the Model X and Model 3 launches and Solar City acquisition. He also held various roles at Apple and J&J earlier in his career and served as a naval officer and aviator for over 9 years.

## Steve Williams, MD, PhD
CSO
Dr. Willams serves as the company’s Chief Scientific Officer. He was previously Chief Medical Officer at Standard Biotools and at SomaLogic where he pioneered the discipline for discovery and validation of predictive, diagnostic and prognostic models using machine-learning applied to large-plex proteomics. 20 such tests were used for drug characterization, safety and efficacy when incorporated in clinical drug trials at Pharma/Biotech and 17 different multivariate tests were validated and translated into regulated healthcare uses. Prior to SomaLogic, Dr. Williams was at Pfizer in the UK and the USA as a clinical triallist in Translational Medicine, and subsequently as VP, Global Clinical Technology. He sat on the National Advisory Council for the National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering, the Executive Committee for the FNIH Biomarkers Consortium, and worked with FDA and PhRMA on developing evidentiary standards for biomarker qualification. Dr. William’s medical training was in London, at Charing Cross and Westminster Medical School, followed by a PhD in medicine/physiology at the same institution and training in Radiology at the University of Newcastle Upon Tyne. Steve is co-inventor on 26 proteomics patents and author/coauthor on multiple foundational proteomics manuscripts.
[ Linkedin ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/justinmcanear/)
## Justin McAnear
CFO
Mr. McAnear serves as the company’s Chief Financial Officer. He brings over 25 years of operational and financial leadership experience across various sectors and was instrumental in taking 10x Genomics public in 2019, serving as its CFO for over five years. Mr. McAnear served for over 3 years as Tesla’s VP of Worldwide Finance and Operations, supporting landmark initiatives such as the Model X and Model 3 launches and Solar City acquisition. He also held various roles at Apple and J&J earlier in his career and served as a naval officer and aviator for over 9 years.

## Steve Williams, MD, PhD
CSO
Dr. Willams serves as the company’s Chief Scientific Officer. He was previously Chief Medical Officer at Standard Biotools and at SomaLogic where he pioneered the discipline for discovery and validation of predictive, diagnostic and prognostic models using machine-learning applied to large-plex proteomics. 20 such tests were used for drug characterization, safety and efficacy when incorporated in clinical drug trials at Pharma/Biotech and 17 different multivariate tests were validated and translated into regulated healthcare uses. Prior to SomaLogic, Dr. Williams was at Pfizer in the UK and the USA as a clinical triallist in Translational Medicine, and subsequently as VP, Global Clinical Technology. He sat on the National Advisory Council for the National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering, the Executive Committee for the FNIH Biomarkers Consortium, and worked with FDA and PhRMA on developing evidentiary standards for biomarker qualification. Dr. William’s medical training was in London, at Charing Cross and Westminster Medical School, followed by a PhD in medicine/physiology at the same institution and training in Radiology at the University of Newcastle Upon Tyne. Steve is co-inventor on 26 proteomics patents and author/coauthor on multiple foundational proteomics manuscripts.
[ Linkedin ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/justinmcanear/)
## Justin McAnear
CFO
Mr. McAnear serves as the company’s Chief Financial Officer. He brings over 25 years of operational and financial leadership experience across various sectors and was instrumental in taking 10x Genomics public in 2019, serving as its CFO for over five years. Mr. McAnear served for over 3 years as Tesla’s VP of Worldwide Finance and Operations, supporting landmark initiatives such as the Model X and Model 3 launches and Solar City acquisition. He also held various roles at Apple and J&J earlier in his career and served as a naval officer and aviator for over 9 years.

## Steve Williams, MD, PhD
CSO
Dr. Willams serves as the company’s Chief Scientific Officer. He was previously Chief Medical Officer at Standard Biotools and at SomaLogic where he pioneered the discipline for discovery and validation of predictive, diagnostic and prognostic models using machine-learning applied to large-plex proteomics. 20 such tests were used for drug characterization, safety and efficacy when incorporated in clinical drug trials at Pharma/Biotech and 17 different multivariate tests were validated and translated into regulated healthcare uses. Prior to SomaLogic, Dr. Williams was at Pfizer in the UK and the USA as a clinical triallist in Translational Medicine, and subsequently as VP, Global Clinical Technology. He sat on the National Advisory Council for the National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering, the Executive Committee for the FNIH Biomarkers Consortium, and worked with FDA and PhRMA on developing evidentiary standards for biomarker qualification. Dr. William’s medical training was in London, at Charing Cross and Westminster Medical School, followed by a PhD in medicine/physiology at the same institution and training in Radiology at the University of Newcastle Upon Tyne. Steve is co-inventor on 26 proteomics patents and author/coauthor on multiple foundational proteomics manuscripts.
[ Linkedin ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/justinmcanear/)
## Justin McAnear
CFO
Mr. McAnear serves as the company’s Chief Financial Officer. He brings over 25 years of operational and financial leadership experience across various sectors and was instrumental in taking 10x Genomics public in 2019, serving as its CFO for over five years. Mr. McAnear served for over 3 years as Tesla’s VP of Worldwide Finance and Operations, supporting landmark initiatives such as the Model X and Model 3 launches and Solar City acquisition. He also held various roles at Apple and J&J earlier in his career and served as a naval officer and aviator for over 9 years.

## Steve Williams, MD, PhD
CSO
Dr. Willams serves as the company’s Chief Scientific Officer. He was previously Chief Medical Officer at Standard Biotools and at SomaLogic where he pioneered the discipline for discovery and validation of predictive, diagnostic and prognostic models using machine-learning applied to large-plex proteomics. 20 such tests were used for drug characterization, safety and efficacy when incorporated in clinical drug trials at Pharma/Biotech and 17 different multivariate tests were validated and translated into regulated healthcare uses. Prior to SomaLogic, Dr. Williams was at Pfizer in the UK and the USA as a clinical triallist in Translational Medicine, and subsequently as VP, Global Clinical Technology. He sat on the National Advisory Council for the National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering, the Executive Committee for the FNIH Biomarkers Consortium, and worked with FDA and PhRMA on developing evidentiary standards for biomarker qualification. Dr. William’s medical training was in London, at Charing Cross and Westminster Medical School, followed by a PhD in medicine/physiology at the same institution and training in Radiology at the University of Newcastle Upon Tyne. Steve is co-inventor on 26 proteomics patents and author/coauthor on multiple foundational proteomics manuscripts.
[ Linkedin ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/justinmcanear/)
## Justin McAnear
CFO
Mr. McAnear serves as the company’s Chief Financial Officer. He brings over 25 years of operational and financial leadership experience across various sectors and was instrumental in taking 10x Genomics public in 2019, serving as its CFO for over five years. Mr. McAnear served for over 3 years as Tesla’s VP of Worldwide Finance and Operations, supporting landmark initiatives such as the Model X and Model 3 launches and Solar City acquisition. He also held various roles at Apple and J&J earlier in his career and served as a naval officer and aviator for over 9 years.

## Steve Williams, MD, PhD
CSO
Dr. Willams serves as the company’s Chief Scientific Officer. He was previously Chief Medical Officer at Standard Biotools and at SomaLogic where he pioneered the discipline for discovery and validation of predictive, diagnostic and prognostic models using machine-learning applied to large-plex proteomics. 20 such tests were used for drug characterization, safety and efficacy when incorporated in clinical drug trials at Pharma/Biotech and 17 different multivariate tests were validated and translated into regulated healthcare uses. Prior to SomaLogic, Dr. Williams was at Pfizer in the UK and the USA as a clinical triallist in Translational Medicine, and subsequently as VP, Global Clinical Technology. He sat on the National Advisory Council for the National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering, the Executive Committee for the FNIH Biomarkers Consortium, and worked with FDA and PhRMA on developing evidentiary standards for biomarker qualification. Dr. William’s medical training was in London, at Charing Cross and Westminster Medical School, followed by a PhD in medicine/physiology at the same institution and training in Radiology at the University of Newcastle Upon Tyne. Steve is co-inventor on 26 proteomics patents and author/coauthor on multiple foundational proteomics manuscripts.

## Justin McAnear
CFO
Mr. McAnear serves as the company’s Chief Financial Officer. He brings over 25 years of operational and financial leadership experience across various sectors and was instrumental in taking 10x Genomics public in 2019, serving as its CFO for over five years. Mr. McAnear served for over 3 years as Tesla’s VP of Worldwide Finance and Operations, supporting landmark initiatives such as the Model X and Model 3 launches and Solar City acquisition. He also held various roles at Apple and J&J earlier in his career and served as a naval officer and aviator for over 9 years.

## Steve Williams, MD, PhD
CSO
Dr. Willams serves as the company’s Chief Scientific Officer. He was previously Chief Medical Officer at Standard Biotools and at SomaLogic where he pioneered the discipline for discovery and validation of predictive, diagnostic and prognostic models using machine-learning applied to large-plex proteomics. 20 such tests were used for drug characterization, safety and efficacy when incorporated in clinical drug trials at Pharma/Biotech and 17 different multivariate tests were validated and translated into regulated healthcare uses. Prior to SomaLogic, Dr. Williams was at Pfizer in the UK and the USA as a clinical triallist in Translational Medicine, and subsequently as VP, Global Clinical Technology. He sat on the National Advisory Council for the National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering, the Executive Committee for the FNIH Biomarkers Consortium, and worked with FDA and PhRMA on developing evidentiary standards for biomarker qualification. Dr. William’s medical training was in London, at Charing Cross and Westminster Medical School, followed by a PhD in medicine/physiology at the same institution and training in Radiology at the University of Newcastle Upon Tyne. Steve is co-inventor on 26 proteomics patents and author/coauthor on multiple foundational proteomics manuscripts.
[ Linkedin ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/justinmcanear/)
## Justin McAnear
CFO
Mr. McAnear serves as the company’s Chief Financial Officer. He brings over 25 years of operational and financial leadership experience across various sectors and was instrumental in taking 10x Genomics public in 2019, serving as its CFO for over five years. Mr. McAnear served for over 3 years as Tesla’s VP of Worldwide Finance and Operations, supporting landmark initiatives such as the Model X and Model 3 launches and Solar City acquisition. He also held various roles at Apple and J&J earlier in his career and served as a naval officer and aviator for over 9 years.

## Steve Williams, MD, PhD
CSO
Dr. Willams serves as the company’s Chief Scientific Officer. He was previously Chief Medical Officer at Standard Biotools and at SomaLogic where he pioneered the discipline for discovery and validation of predictive, diagnostic and prognostic models using machine-learning applied to large-plex proteomics. 20 such tests were used for drug characterization, safety and efficacy when incorporated in clinical drug trials at Pharma/Biotech and 17 different multivariate tests were validated and translated into regulated healthcare uses. Prior to SomaLogic, Dr. Williams was at Pfizer in the UK and the USA as a clinical triallist in Translational Medicine, and subsequently as VP, Global Clinical Technology. He sat on the National Advisory Council for the National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering, the Executive Committee for the FNIH Biomarkers Consortium, and worked with FDA and PhRMA on developing evidentiary standards for biomarker qualification. Dr. William’s medical training was in London, at Charing Cross and Westminster Medical School, followed by a PhD in medicine/physiology at the same institution and training in Radiology at the University of Newcastle Upon Tyne. Steve is co-inventor on 26 proteomics patents and author/coauthor on multiple foundational proteomics manuscripts.
[ Linkedin ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/justinmcanear/)
## Justin McAnear
CFO
Mr. McAnear serves as the company’s Chief Financial Officer. He brings over 25 years of operational and financial leadership experience across various sectors and was instrumental in taking 10x Genomics public in 2019, serving as its CFO for over five years. Mr. McAnear served for over 3 years as Tesla’s VP of Worldwide Finance and Operations, supporting landmark initiatives such as the Model X and Model 3 launches and Solar City acquisition. He also held various roles at Apple and J&J earlier in his career and served as a naval officer and aviator for over 9 years.

## Steve Williams, MD, PhD
CSO
Dr. Willams serves as the company’s Chief Scientific Officer. He was previously Chief Medical Officer at Standard Biotools and at SomaLogic where he pioneered the discipline for discovery and validation of predictive, diagnostic and prognostic models using machine-learning applied to large-plex proteomics. 20 such tests were used for drug characterization, safety and efficacy when incorporated in clinical drug trials at Pharma/Biotech and 17 different multivariate tests were validated and translated into regulated healthcare uses. Prior to SomaLogic, Dr. Williams was at Pfizer in the UK and the USA as a clinical triallist in Translational Medicine, and subsequently as VP, Global Clinical Technology. He sat on the National Advisory Council for the National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering, the Executive Committee for the FNIH Biomarkers Consortium, and worked with FDA and PhRMA on developing evidentiary standards for biomarker qualification. Dr. William’s medical training was in London, at Charing Cross and Westminster Medical School, followed by a PhD in medicine/physiology at the same institution and training in Radiology at the University of Newcastle Upon Tyne. Steve is co-inventor on 26 proteomics patents and author/coauthor on multiple foundational proteomics manuscripts.
[ Linkedin ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/justinmcanear/)
## Justin McAnear
CFO
Mr. McAnear serves as the company’s Chief Financial Officer. He brings over 25 years of operational and financial leadership experience across various sectors and was instrumental in taking 10x Genomics public in 2019, serving as its CFO for over five years. Mr. McAnear served for over 3 years as Tesla’s VP of Worldwide Finance and Operations, supporting landmark initiatives such as the Model X and Model 3 launches and Solar City acquisition. He also held various roles at Apple and J&J earlier in his career and served as a naval officer and aviator for over 9 years.

## Steve Williams, MD, PhD
CSO
Dr. Willams serves as the company’s Chief Scientific Officer. He was previously Chief Medical Officer at Standard Biotools and at SomaLogic where he pioneered the discipline for discovery and validation of predictive, diagnostic and prognostic models using machine-learning applied to large-plex proteomics. 20 such tests were used for drug characterization, safety and efficacy when incorporated in clinical drug trials at Pharma/Biotech and 17 different multivariate tests were validated and translated into regulated healthcare uses. Prior to SomaLogic, Dr. Williams was at Pfizer in the UK and the USA as a clinical triallist in Translational Medicine, and subsequently as VP, Global Clinical Technology. He sat on the National Advisory Council for the National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering, the Executive Committee for the FNIH Biomarkers Consortium, and worked with FDA and PhRMA on developing evidentiary standards for biomarker qualification. Dr. William’s medical training was in London, at Charing Cross and Westminster Medical School, followed by a PhD in medicine/physiology at the same institution and training in Radiology at the University of Newcastle Upon Tyne. Steve is co-inventor on 26 proteomics patents and author/coauthor on multiple foundational proteomics manuscripts.
[ Linkedin ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/justinmcanear/)
## Justin McAnear
CFO
Mr. McAnear serves as the company’s Chief Financial Officer. He brings over 25 years of operational and financial leadership experience across various sectors and was instrumental in taking 10x Genomics public in 2019, serving as its CFO for over five years. Mr. McAnear served for over 3 years as Tesla’s VP of Worldwide Finance and Operations, supporting landmark initiatives such as the Model X and Model 3 launches and Solar City acquisition. He also held various roles at Apple and J&J earlier in his career and served as a naval officer and aviator for over 9 years.

# Neurodegenerative Disease Biomarker Detection Using an Ultra-Sensitive Profiling Method
#### Featuring:
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/GENlogo_ColorBackground_062618_200.png)
#### **![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/HenrikZetterbergHS-150x150.png)Henrik Zetterberg, MD, PhD**
Professor of Neurochemistry,  
University of Gothenburg  
  

#### **![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/DougHinerfeld-150x150.png)Doug Hinerfeld, PhD**
Senior Director of Application Support,  
Alamar Biosciences
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://www.workcast.cohttps://www.workcast.com/register?cpak=3018982020663234)
Brain-derived biomarkers of neurodegenerative diseases are important targets for new therapies. In the context of Alzheimer’s disease, scientists are exploring the use of protein biomarkers for early diagnosis, screening, prognosis prediction, and disease monitoring. But these markers are often present at very low concentrations in plasma or serum, much too low for most existing proteomics assays to detect and measure.
In this GEN webinar, Henrik Zetterberg, MD, PhD, an expert in Alzheimer’s disease, will discuss his efforts to discover and validate blood-based biomarkers for various CNS disorders. During his presentation, he will share data from his evaluation of the NULISA immunoassay platform’s ability to detect biomarkers of Alzheimer’s disease from serum. You will also hear from Doug Hinerfeld, PhD, who will discuss the NULISA platform’s multiplex and protein marker detection capabilities in more depth.

## Steve Williams, MD, PhD
CSO
Dr. Willams serves as the company’s Chief Scientific Officer. He was previously Chief Medical Officer at Standard Biotools and at SomaLogic where he pioneered the discipline for discovery and validation of predictive, diagnostic and prognostic models using machine-learning applied to large-plex proteomics. 20 such tests were used for drug characterization, safety and efficacy when incorporated in clinical drug trials at Pharma/Biotech and 17 different multivariate tests were validated and translated into regulated healthcare uses. Prior to SomaLogic, Dr. Williams was at Pfizer in the UK and the USA as a clinical triallist in Translational Medicine, and subsequently as VP, Global Clinical Technology. He sat on the National Advisory Council for the National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering, the Executive Committee for the FNIH Biomarkers Consortium, and worked with FDA and PhRMA on developing evidentiary standards for biomarker qualification. Dr. William’s medical training was in London, at Charing Cross and Westminster Medical School, followed by a PhD in medicine/physiology at the same institution and training in Radiology at the University of Newcastle Upon Tyne. Steve is co-inventor on 26 proteomics patents and author/coauthor on multiple foundational proteomics manuscripts.
[ Linkedin ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/justinmcanear/)
## Justin McAnear
CFO
Mr. McAnear serves as the company’s Chief Financial Officer. He brings over 25 years of operational and financial leadership experience across various sectors and was instrumental in taking 10x Genomics public in 2019, serving as its CFO for over five years. Mr. McAnear served for over 3 years as Tesla’s VP of Worldwide Finance and Operations, supporting landmark initiatives such as the Model X and Model 3 launches and Solar City acquisition. He also held various roles at Apple and J&J earlier in his career and served as a naval officer and aviator for over 9 years.

# A Blood Test for Alzheimer’s Disease – Thinking Beyond a Diagnosis
#### Featuring:
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/virtual_event_profile_image_99a0dd4eb5a626def38ae9f13e0f652fc610ec8f_5771-300x150.jpg)
####  ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/NickAshton100px.png)**Nicholas Ashton, PhD**
Associate Professor of Neurochemistry  
University of Gothenburg
#### **![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/AlexForrestHay_crop2_100px.jpg)Alex Forrest-Hay**
VP of Sales  
Alamar Biosciences
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://www.labroots.com/webinar/blood-test-alzheimer-s-disease-thinking-beyond-diagnosis)
The advancement in ultra-sensitive immunoassays and highly specific immunoprecipitation mass spectrometry (IPMS) methods, complimented by an increasing number of well-characterised research cohorts adhering to a biological definition of disease, have substantially contributed to the rapid development of reliability quantifying key targets in blood plasma or serum samples. In Alzheimer’s disease (AD), measures of phosphorylated tau (p-tau), particularly p-tau217, have now shown great utility in identifying cerebral pathology at all stages of the disease continuum. Thus, it is anticipated that plasma p-tau217 will be an important component of patient management and treatments decisions related to AD. Yet, there remains a multitude of biomarker applications in AD, and related disorders, where plasma p-tau217 may not be fully sufficient. Therefore, a new period of proteomic biomarker discovery has begun, centered around p-tau, NfL, and GFAP, to address these needs.
This session will briefly overview the rapid development of blood biomarkers for AD, with a focus on phosphorylated tau. The talk will then highlight areas of need in biomarkers development, in the era of disease-modifying trials. We will conclude by looking at the capabilities of NULISA at the singleplex and multiplex level, and case-studies in how this novel technology may begin to address new biomarkers challenages that are emerging.
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://www.labroots.com/webinar/blood-test-alzheimer-s-disease-thinking-beyond-diagnosis)
###### FOR RESEARCH USE ONLY. Not for use in diagnostic procedures.

metadata.title: 15th Annual Traumatic Brain Injury Conference - Alamar Biosciences
metadata.description: Join Alamar at the 15th Annual Traumatic Brain Injury Conference in Boston, MA, May 5-6, 2025. This conference brings together researchers and clinicians from industry, academia, the military and government to present ground-breaking research in a variety of areas related to traumatic brain injury.

#### Richland, WA
#### 2025 SPONSOR
##### Predictive Phenomics: Advancing Molecular Science for Controlling the Phenome
The conference will consist of keynotes, invited talks, poster sessions, PNNL tours, and a forum for scientists to present research on approaches to study the molecular basis of biological function with a vision to better understand and predict how genomes interact with their environment to produce phenomes.

metadata.title: 8th Venusberg Meeting on Neuroinflammation - Alamar Biosciences
metadata.description: Cerebral immune activation at the crossroads of healthy aging, senescence and neurodegeneration encompassing basic, clinical, methodological and emerging perspectives and including internationally renowned scientists with expertise across a wide range of domains, as main speakers.
metadata.author: April Falcone
metadata.og:title: 8th Venusberg Meeting on Neuroinflammation 15th Annual Traumatic Brain Injury Conference
metadata.og:description: Join Alamar at the 15th Annual Traumatic Brain Injury Conference in Boston, MA, May 5-6, 2025. This conference brings together researchers and clinicians from industry, academia, the military and government to present ground-breaking research in a variety of areas related to traumatic brain injury.

# The Role of Inflammation in Neurological Disease Manifestations – Symposium
#### ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/FrieburgBanner.png)
#### **May 24, 2025  
**
**Medical Center University of Freiburg**  
**Lecture Hall – Department of Gynaecology**
Hugstetter Str. 55, 79106 Freiburg
#### **– SPONSOR & Exhibitor –**
We are pleased to support the inaugural symposium, **“The Role of Inflammation in Neurological Disease Manifestations,”** on **May 24, 2025**. This event marks the official welcome of **Prof. Dr. Heinz Wiendl** as the new Head of the Department, following his transition from Münster in October 2024.
The symposium will bring together leading international experts to explore the evolving understanding of inflammation’s impact on the central and peripheral nervous systems. Topics will include multiple sclerosis (MS), neuroimmunology, disease progression, and innovative diagnostic and therapeutic approaches. Speakers such as **Amit Bar-Or (University of Pennsylvania)** , **Xavier Montalban (Barcelona)** , **Ludwig Kappos (Basel)** , and **Sergio Baranzini (UCSF)** will share insights across five thematic sessions.
The event will take place at the Medical Center – University of Freiburg and is open to clinicians, researchers, and students in neurology, immunology, and related fields.
[ VIEW EVENT ](https://www.uniklinik-freiburg.de/neurology-symposium.html#c268407)
###### FOR RESEARCH USE ONLY. Not for use in diagnostic procedures.

metadata.title: Sanofi Global Analytical Symposium - Alamar Biosciences
metadata.description: Join Alamar at the 11th Annual Sanofi Global Analytical Symposium, June 4-5, in Cambridge, MA.
metadata.author: Jessica Pitts
metadata.og:title: Sanofi Global Analytical Symposium 11th Annual Sanofi Global Analytical Symposium
metadata.og:description: The 11th Annual Sanofi Global Analytical Symposium will unite Sanofi Analytical Scientists from the Small Molecule, Biologics, and Vaccine divisions. In 2025, the symposium will cover topics such as AI applications in Research, CMC, and Clinical Trials, Immunology and Inflammation, LNP/RNA, Vaccines (both traditional platforms and RNA-based), and Biomarkers.

# Sanofi Global Analytical Symposium
#### ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/SGAS2025_Banner-1.webp)
#### **June 4-5  
Sanofi Cambridge Crossing  
Cambridge, MA  
**
#### **SILVER SPONSOR**
#### Booth #20
We are excited to participate in the **11th Annual Sanofi Global Analytical Symposium** , joining over 300 scientists from Sanofi’s Small Molecule, Biologics, and Vaccine divisions, exploring advances in analytical science.
The symposium provides a valuable forum for engaging with the Sanofi Analytical Sciences community through scientific talks, plenary sessions, live poster presentations, and vendor exhibits—offering opportunities to highlight technologies like [**NULISA™**](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/nulisa-assays-for-immunology/) and contribute to ongoing discussions around analytical innovation and emerging therapeutic platforms.
###### FOR RESEARCH USE ONLY. Not for use in diagnostic procedures.

# Neurotrauma 2025
#### ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/NNS2025-Logo_long_black-qrzxzyv0gcfp05bcbfxixckcvbbu036z9346mafshs.png)
####  **June 15-18 | Philadelphia Marriott Downtown  
****Philadelphia, P****A  
**
#### **2025 SUPPORTER**
#### Booth #31
Alamar Biosciences is honored to support the Neurotrauma Symposium, the premier forum advancing research and care for traumatic brain injury (TBI) and spinal cord injury.
This annual meeting brings together leading scientists and clinicians to share breakthroughs across basic, translational, and clinical neurotrauma research. As part of our commitment to neurological disease research, we’re showcasing how our ultra-sensitive, multiplexed NULISA™ technology is powering new insights into blood-based biomarkers of TBI—enabling earlier detection, deeper understanding, and better outcomes.
[ Learn More ](https://www.neurotrauma-symposium.org/)

# EUPA 2025
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/EUPA-2025-St-Malo-1024x451.png)
## June 16-20 | Saint Malo, France  

#### EXHIBITION SPONSOR
The **EuPA 2025** , Conference of the **European Proteomics Association** will be held in Saint-Malo, France this year, from June 16 to 20. This event gathers a large portion of the Proteomics and Mass Spectrometry community attracted by an outstanding scientific program covering the most up to date aspects of the disciplines. Explore cutting-edge proteomics and join our symposium on NULISA technology for biomarker detection across biological matrices.
**Visit us at Booth #24**
#### Exhibitors Workshop
#### Thursday, 19 June | 13:30-14:20 CEST
Main Auditorium
**Application of NULISA technology for biomarker detection across multiple biological matrix**
**![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/HS-Nicolas-Pradeilles-300x300.png)**
######  **Nicolas Pradeilles**  
Hospital Technician specializing in immunoassays  
CHU de Montpellier
**NULISA: Fully automated ultra-sensitive fluid biomarker platform**
**![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/MIkeEvans100px.png)**
######  **Michael Evans**  
Director of Sales, EMEA  
Alamar Biosciences

# 3rd Annual Symposium on Human Proteome and Health, Oxford 2025
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Oxford-Population-Health-logo.png)
## June 24-25 | Oxford, UK  

#### EXHIBITION SPONSOR
Taking place from **June 24–25, 2025, at Rhodes House, Oxford,** this esteemed gathering brings together leading minds from academia and industry to explore the latest advancements in proteomics and their applications in health and disease.
Looking forward to connecting with peers, partners, and pioneers as we explore where proteomics goes next.
#### Researcher Presentation
#### Tuesday, 24 June | 11:35-11:50 BST
**Alamar-based proteomics in REACT and Airwave studies**
**![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/HS-Ioanna_Tzoulaki-300x300.png)**
######  **Professor Ioanna Tzoulaki, PhD.  
** Imperial Chair in Chronic Disease Epidemiology  
Imperial College London
#### Panel Discussion
#### Tuesday, 24 June | 13:15-14:15 BST
**Application of NULISA technology for biomarker detection across multiple biological matrix**
**![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/AlexForrestHay_crop2.png-300x300.jpg)**
######  **Alex Forrest-Hay**

Alamar Biosciences

# Translational Immunology School – TIS2025
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/DGFL-logo.png)
## July 3-5 | Potsdam, Germany
#### EXHIBITION SPONSOR
Taking place from **July 3–5, 2025, at Kongresshotel Potsdam,** we join leading minds in immunology at the Translational Immunology School, where academic researchers, clinicians, and industry experts come together to explore the latest advances in diagnostics, immune therapies, and translational research.
From cutting-edge technologies to breakthroughs in stem cell and gene therapy, this event offers a unique platform to exchange ideas in a collaborative setting.
#### Sponsored Talk
####  Thursday, 03 July | 17:30-18:50 CEST
**Ultrasensitive Proteomics (NULISA) for Low-Abundance Inflammatory Biomarkers**
**![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/HS-Muamar-Hodzic-300x300.png)**
######  **Muamer Hodzic.  
** Alamar Biosciences
[ Conference Page ](https://dgfi.org/akademie-fuer-immunologie/translational-school/)
###### FOR RESEARCH USE ONLY. Not for use in diagnostic procedures.

## Set sail with Alamar for an evening of innovation, connection, and skyline views
####   
Tuesday, July 29 | 6:00 – 9:00 pm
**Toronto Yachts  
** _5 Queens Quay W, Toronto, ON M5J 2H1, Canada  
*10 minute drive from the Metro Toronto Convention Centre  
_
###### Dinner buffet and drinks will be served.
After a full day at AAIC, join global thought leaders, key collaborators, and the Alamar Biosciences team for an evening on Lake Ontario aboard a luxury mega yacht. Enjoy meaningful conversations and connections around the future of Alzheimer’s disease research—all while taking in the Toronto skyline over dinner, drinks, and great company.

# International Congress of Immunology (IUIS) 2025
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/iuis-LOGO-cropped-1024x435.png)
#### EXHIBITION SPONSOR
Attending the **IUIS 2025 congress in Vienna** offers a unique opportunity to engage with cutting-edge immunology research, network with global experts, and advance your career. The congress, hosted by the**International Union of Immunological Societies (IUIS)** , will feature a diverse scientific program, including presentations from rising stars and opportunities for in-depth discussions.
Grab a lunch and join us on Wednesday 20th August for a workshop highlighting real-data insights gained from the NULISA platform, from two Europe-based researchers. 
**Visit us at Booth #71**
#### Exhibitors Workshop
#### Wednesday, 20 August | 12:30-13:15 CEST
Room 1.34
**Attomolar-Sensitive Profiling of Inflammatory Proteins Reveals Novel Mechanisms of Immune Response**
From environmental exposure to immunotherapy, the in-event **Alamar Biosciences sponsored session** explores how ultra-sensitive, high-plex proteomics is accelerating translational immunology and uncovering clinically relevant immune mechanisms. Joined by key researchers in immunology research, the session showcases how attomolar-level protein detection is redefining what’s possible in biomarker discovery and immune system profiling.
If your research aims to inform the clinic, this session will show how next-generation proteomics is making that leap—from signal to significance.
**NULISA: Fully automated ultra-sensitive fluid biomarker platform**
**![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/MIkeEvans100px.png)**
######  **Michael Evans**  
Director of Sales, EMEA  
Alamar Biosciences
**Molecular signatures of environmental influence in the circulation**
**![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/HS-Cezmi-Adkis-300x300.png)**
######  **Prof. Cezmi Akdis, MD.** Director of the Swiss Institute of Allergy and Asthma University of Zurich, Switzerland   
Research (SIAF)
**Systems immunology reveals the first-week cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying successful insect-venom allergen-specific immunotherapy**
**![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/HS-Feng-Hefeng-300x300.png)**
######  **Dr. Feng HeFeng, PhD, ADR**  
Senior Researcher, Translational and Clinical Immunology Luxembourg Institute of Health, Luxembourg
[ Visit Conference Site ](https://iuis2025.org/)
###### FOR RESEARCH USE ONLY. Not for use in diagnostic procedures.

# Oxford Global Biomarkers & Precision Medicine 2025
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/OG-Biomarkers-and-Precision-Medicine-2025-logo-1024x576.png)
#### BRONZE SPONSOR
**Biomarkers & Precision Medicine UK** 2025 takes place 30 September–1 October at the QEII Centre in London, marking the 20th year of Oxford Global’s flagship conference. The event brings together leading scientists, pharma and biotech innovators, diagnostics experts, and translational researchers to **advance biomarker discovery, validation, and clinical application**.
For Alamar, this is a key forum to connect with the biomarker community. Our mission is to equip researchers with tools to reliably measure low-abundance biomarkers in blood and other fluids — enabling breakthroughs in**neurodegeneration, inflammation, and disease progression**. The discussions at this event mirror the challenges we address every day: detection sensitivity and assay validation, that drive discovery forward.
**Visit us at Booth #37**
#### SPONSORED TALK
#### TRACK 1 | Biomarkers identification & Validation: Neuroscience & Co-Morbidity
#### Wednesday, 01 October | 14:30-14:55 BST
Conference Room 1
**Novel blood-based proteomic signatures across multiple neurodegenerative diseases**
Dr. Malpetti will share how multiplex proteomic analysis of Cambridge-based cohorts is advancing our understanding of **neurodegeneration and inflammation in conditions** beyond Alzheimer’s disease, including **frontotemporal dementia (FTD) and progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP)**. She will highlight how blood biomarkers such as pTau, NfL, and inflammation markers are reshaping our view of disease progression, multi-etiology dementia, and survival prediction.
Attendees will gain valuable insight into the translational impact of large-scale proteomic screening and how highly sensitive blood-based assays can drive earlier detection and more precise disease monitoring across multiple neurodegenerative disorders.
**![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Maura_Malpetti-300x298.jpg)**
######  **Maura Malpetti, PhD.**  
Race Against Dementia ARUK Fellow, Senior Research Associate  
UK DRI at Cambridge
[ Visit Conference Site ](https://oxfordglobal.com/precision-medicine/events/biomarkers-precision-medicine)

# 5th Crick International Cancer Conference
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/The_Francis_Crick_Institute_logo214b98f5-34f9-4682-8e26-2444e27a8e31-276x300.png)
**5-7 October 2025 | London UK**
#### EXHIBITOR
We’re proud to be an exhibition sponsor at the**5th Crick International Cancer Conference,** on 5–7 October 2025 at the Francis Crick Institute in London. Gathering leading cancer biologists, clinicians and translational researchers, this event event discusses themes such as tumour metabolism, immune-cancer interactions, cellular state regulation, metastasis, therapy resistance.
**Alamar’s core expertise in fluid biomarker analysis** speaks directly to the conference’s translational agenda including liquid biopsy assays, proteomic and metabolomic markers, and dynamic biomarker tracking across therapy time-courses. We look forward to engaging with researchers pushing the frontiers of oncology, demonstrating how our technologies can accelerate biomarker discovery, validation, and ultimately translation into improving patient outcomes.
[ Visit Conference Site ](https://www.crick.ac.uk/whats-on/5th-crick-international-cancer-conference)
###### FOR RESEARCH USE ONLY. Not for use in diagnostic procedures.

# 3rd Qatar Proteomics Conference
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/qpc_new-300x300.png)
**13-15 October 20245 | Doha, Qatar**
#### BRONZE SPONSOR
The**3rd Qatar Proteomics Conference** brings together leading academic scientists, bioinformaticians, translational researchers, and proteomics technologists to share the latest advances in mass spectrometry, affinity-based platforms, cross-omics, and disease-based applications (e.g. diabetes, infections).
**Are you working with fluid biomarkers?** At Alamar, we focus on enabling the detection and quantification of low-abundance proteins in blood and biological fluids — a capability that complements the proteomics tools and methods showcased at Qatar Proteomics. We look forward to engaging with the research community, exchanging insights on **assay sensitivity and multiplexing, and seeing where biomarker discovery meets clinical translation** in the region.
[ Visit Conference Site ](https://www.qatarproteomics.com/)
###### FOR RESEARCH USE ONLY. Not for use in diagnostic procedures.

# Biomarkers of Aging 2025 Conference
####  ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/BoACLogoUpdated-WhiteBackground1.png)**October 20-21**  
Harvard University, Boston, MA
#### **– 2025 SPONSOR –**
#### **Unlock the secrets of biological aging with gold standard sensitivity**
The **Biomarkers of Aging Consortium Conference** brings together leading scientists and innovators advancing the understanding of biological aging. As anti-aging therapies move closer to the clinic, the need for standardized, validated biomarkers has never been greater.
[**NULISA™ technology**](https://alamarbio.com/technology/nulisa-platform/) delivers _gold-standard sensitivity_ for the detection of 250+ key aging-related proteins, revealing proteomic signatures that define the biology of aging. By enabling researchers to uncover new biomarkers and pathways, NULISA accelerates progress toward reliable tools for measuring aging and evaluating the impact of longevity interventions.
[ Visit Conference Site ](https://www.agingconsortium.org/conference-home)
###### FOR RESEARCH USE ONLY. Not for use in diagnostic procedures.

# ELRIG Drug Discovery 2025
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/ELRIG-DD25-square-300x300.jpg)
##### 21-22 October 2025 | Liverpool, UK
#### CO-EXHIBITOR with ELEMENT BIOSCIENCES
We’re excited to be part of **ELRIG Drug Discovery 2025** (21-22 October in Liverpool) — Europe’s go-to free-to-attend life sciences festival covering themes from ‘omics and AI to oncology and translational drug pipelines. [elrig.org](https://elrig.org/portfolio/drug-discovery-2025/) This event is It’s a **free-to-attend** , open-access conference that fuses rigorous science with broad accessibility, drawing over 3,000 delegates, 200+ exhibitors, and more than 150 talks across ~14 scientific tracks. 
Our expertise in **fluid biomarker analysis** (for example liquid biopsies and proteomic signatures) dovetails with the drug discovery community’s need to monitor disease state, pharmacodynamics, early response, and resistance mechanisms in real time.
We look forward to engaging with discovery scientists, showcasing how our platform can help **accelerate biomarker-driven decision making** across the therapeutic development pipeline.
[ Visit Conference Website ](https://elrig.org/portfolio/drug-discovery-2025/)
###### FOR RESEARCH USE ONLY. Not for use in diagnostic procedures.

# 7th Inflammasome Therapeutics Summit
#### ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/58927-7th-Inflammasome-Therapeutics-Summit-COL-2-2048x431-1-1024x216.png)
#### November 4-6  
Boston, MA
#### **– LEAD PARTNER –**
#### **Partner Presentation**
#### November 5 | 10:00-10:30 am
#### **NULISA Assay Platform  
**
**_Highest sensitivity single- to high-plex biomarker analysis of soluble proteins and fluid biomarkers in preclinical models and for clinical development_**
  * NULISA™ combines ultra-sensitive femtogram level detection with barcode-based high-plex biomarker analysis.
  * Broad matrix compatibility and highest sensitivity in plasma, serum, synovial fluid, nasal lining fluid, sputum, lysates and other matrices.
  * Single-, low-, and high-plex assays run fully automated on the ARGO HT System.
  * Custom assay development kits for end-users and CRO development services.
  * NULISAseq™ Inflammation Panel 250 provides comprehensive analysis of 250 cytokines, chemokines and other immune regulatory proteins from 25uL of biofluid.
  * NULISAseq Inflammation Panel AQ provides 156 absolute quantification measurements
  * NULISA CNS Disease Panel is unmatched for high-plex analysis of hundreds (130+) of neuroinflammation, vascular, and synaptic dysfunction, and proteinopathy biomarker
  * NULISAseq Mouse Panel 120 for disease model analysis of immune, neuro and growth factors.
  * Unique ability to translate multiplexed discoveries to single and low-plex biomarker assays – same antibodies, same ARGO HT.
  * NULISA IVD and ARGO DX in development with funding from Gates Ventures and DxA.

metadata.title: Unraveling Ankylosing Spondylitis: Integrating Proteomics with Global Genetic Meta-Analysis - Alamar Biosciences
metadata.description: In this GEN webinar, Dr. Nicholas Harvey, (Kings College London), will present findings from the largest genome-wide association study (GWAS) meta-analysis of AS to date, integrating data across diverse ancestries (e.g. European, East Asian, Turkish, and Iranian) and multiple omic layers, including the transcriptome, proteome, Mendelian randomization, and microbiome.
metadata.author: Jessica Pitts
metadata.og:title: Unraveling Ankylosing Spondylitis: Integrating Proteomics with Global Genetic Meta-Analysis
metadata.og:description: In this GEN webinar, expert speaker, Nicholas Harvey, PhD, will present findings from the largest genome-wide association study (GWAS) meta-analysis of AS to date, integrating data across diverse ancestries (e.g. European, East Asian, Turkish, and Iranian) and multiple omic layers, including the transcriptome, proteome, Mendelian randomization, and microbiome.

# Unraveling Ankylosing Spondylitis: Integrating Proteomics with Global Genetic Meta-Analysis
## UPCOMING WEBINAR Tuesday, November 11
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/GENlogo_ColorBackground_062618-300x53.webp)
### 8:00 am PT / 11:00 am ET / 4:00 pm GMT
#### Featuring:
#### **![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Nicholas-Harvey-KCL-150x150.jpg)**
#### Nicholas Harvey, PhD
##### Postdoctoral Research Associate  
King’s College London
[ View On Demand ](https://www.genengnews.com/multimedia/webinars/unraveling-ankylosing-spondylitis-integrating-proteomics-with-global-genetic-meta-analysis/?utm_source=webpage)
Ankylosing Spondylitis (AS) is a debilitating, immune-mediated disease which causes inflammation of the joints between the vertebrae, leading to stiffness, pain, and eventually fusion of the spine. The underpinnings of AS are highly complex and span genetic, environmental, and immunologic factors. Insights from proteomic analysis helps with mapping risk factors and identifying potential therapeutic targets.
In this GEN webinar, our expert speaker, Nicholas Harvey, PhD, will present findings from the largest genome-wide association study (GWAS) meta-analysis of AS to date, integrating data across diverse ancestries (e.g. European, East Asian, Turkish, and Iranian) and multiple omic layers, including the transcriptome, proteome, Mendelian randomization, and microbiome. During the webinar, you will gain new insights into AS pathogenesis, therapeutic challenges, and novel avenues for precision medicine.
**Key takeaways:**
  * The identification of novel AS loci and signals, including 27 new genome-wide significant loci and 86 independent non-MHC associations
  * The connection between AS risk and secretor status in the gut microbiome
  * The impact of longer leukocyte telomeres on AS susceptibility
  * The role of cytokine biology in therapy efficacy
  * How to prioritize genes by applying fine-mapping to highlight causal variants


###### FOR RESEARCH USE ONLY. Not for use in diagnostic procedures.

## Join Us: An Evening with Alamar Biosciences at CTAD 2025
####   
Monday, December 1 | 7:30 – 10:00 pm
**Lumi Rooftop**  
366 Fifth Ave, San Diego, CA 92101  
 _*0.5 mile walk from the conference_
After a full day at **CTAD** , join colleagues, collaborators, and the Alamar Biosciences team for an evening at Lumi Rooftop in San Diego’s Gaslamp District. Enjoy meaningful conversations around the latest advances in Alzheimer’s disease research, including Alamar’s newly launched **NULISAqpcr™ BD-pTau217 Assay,** a breakthrough advancing precision in biomarker discovery—while taking in rooftop views over cocktails, fresh sushi and Japanese-inspired dishes, and great company.

# HUPO 2025
#### ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/HUPO2025_logo_color_compact-1024x490-1.png)
#### **2025 EXHIBITOR**
#### Booth #401
#### Industry Lunch Seminar
#### Tuesday, November 11 | 12:15 – 1:15 pm  

##### **Beyond Neurofilament: ALS Plasma Biomarkers**
**![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Eleanor-Thomas-Emory.png)**
######  **Eleanor Thomas, MD, PhD  
** _Assistant Professor of Neurology  
Emory University_
Dr. Eleanor Thomas of Emory University will present new findings on ALS plasma biomarkers using the ultra-sensitive NULISA™ platform. While neurofilament light (NEFL) and heavy chains (NEFH) remain reliable indicators, her team identified elevated levels of phosphorylated tau proteins (pTau181, pTau217, pTau231) and phosphorylated TDP-43 (pTDP-43) in ALS patient plasma. These markers, typically associated with Alzheimer’s disease, correlated with disease onset, progression, and severity—particularly in spinal-onset ALS. Notably, pTDP-43 was also detected in some asymptomatic C9orf72 mutation carriers, suggesting potential for early detection. Strong correlations between NEFL, pTau, and pTDP-43 point to overlapping neurodegenerative mechanisms. These findings support the use of multiplexed plasma biomarkers for diagnosis, monitoring, and clinical trial stratification in ALS.
## Oral & Poster Presentations
  * **PV.01.048** : Using Proteomics in Mendelian Randomization and Randomized Controlled Trial Settings to Understand the Aetiology of Multiple Myeloma – **Lucy Goudswaard, University of Bristol**
    * November 10, 2025, 1:15 PM – 3:15 PM
  * **OS13.05:** Plasma Proteomic Signatures Predict Progression-Free Survival in NSCLC Patients Undergoing Anti-PD-L1 and Chemotherapy – **Yuehan Feng, Biognosys, University of Fribourg**
    * November 11, 2025, 10:20 AM – 11:50 AM
  * **OS29.04:** Comprehensive Cross-Platform Evaluation of Eight Plasma Proteomics Technologies Using a Single Cohort –**Sara Ahadi, Alkahest**
    * November 12, 2025, 3:15 PM – 4:20 PM

# 9th Dermatology Drug Development Summit
#### ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/59637-9th-Dermatology-Drug-Development-Summit-Logo-Colour-Annual-1024x215.png)
#### November 18-20  
Boston, MA
#### **– 2025 PARTNER –**
#### Uncover Disease Heterogeneity within Dermatology to Discover Novel Targets, Ensure A Commercially Viable Clinical Strategy, and Deliver Novel Therapeutics to Market with Superior Safety & Efficacy
Join Alamar and industry leaders, to explore disease heterogeneity, novel therapies and MoA, safety and the evolving reg landscape, as well as deep dives into the latest preclinical and clinical findings across rare and common disease (including AD, Psoriasis, HS, Vitiligo, Pemphigus Nodularis, Bullous Pemphigoid, Alopecia Areata).
[ Visit Conference Site ](https://dermatology-drugdevelopment.com/)

records.title: Brain-Derived p-Tau and Biobanks: A Q&A with Prof. Henrik Zetterberg on Next-Generation Alzheimer’s Blood Biomarkers - Alamar Biosciences

metadata.title: Brain-Derived p-Tau and Biobanks: A Q&A with Prof. Henrik Zetterberg on Next-Generation Alzheimer’s Blood Biomarkers - Alamar Biosciences
metadata.description: Explore how brain-derived p-tau217 is revolutionizing Alzheimer’s blood biomarkers, and learn how biobanks can validate large-scale cohorts with Prof. Henrik Zetterberg.
metadata.author: April Falcone
metadata.og:title: Brain-Derived p-Tau and Biobanks: A Q&A with Prof. Henrik Zetterberg on Next-Generation Alzheimer’s Blood Biomarkers Brain-Derived Versions of Phospho-Tau Make Better Markers
metadata.og:description: Alamar Biosciences showcased its ultra-sensitive NULISA™ technology at AAIC 2025, debuting BD p-tau isoforms and a 123-protein mouse CNS panel to advance Alzheimer’s biomarker discovery and deepen understanding of brain pathology.

## Abstract
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Interview-with-Prof.-Zetterberg-1024x683-1.jpg)
[Henrik Zetterberg](https://www.gu.se/en/about/find-staff/henrikzetterberg) is Professor of Neurochemistry at University College London (UCL) and at the University of Gothenburg, and a Senior Consultant in Clinical Chemistry at Sahlgrenska University Hospital. His research focuses on fluid biomarkers for neurodegenerative diseases, especially Alzheimer’s disease.
For years, total tau in blood proved too noisy to be clinically useful: much of it comes from the body’s periphery rather than the brain, muddying Alzheimer’s disease (AD) readouts. New assays that selectively measure brain derived tau—and, specifically, brain-derived phosphotau217 (ptau217), aim to fix that. For biobanks, the implications are immediate: large cohorts with stored samples and imaging/cognition data are uniquely positioned to validate cut points, compare against PET (an imaging technique that uses radiotracers to visualize biological processes in the body), and assess performance in real-world populations.

## Abstract
**#15 Xiao-Jun Ma, Phd** – CTO, Alamar Biosciences.
The Healthcare Technology Report is pleased to announce The Top 25 BioTech and Life Sciences Executives of 2025. This year’s awardees represent a cross-section of leaders driving scientific, operational, and technological progress across the life sciences industry. They include founders, CEOs, and senior executives at companies developing next-generation therapeutics, building AI-enabled discovery platforms, advancing high-sensitivity diagnostics, and reimagining clinical development and manufacturing. From early-stage ventures to global biopharmaceutical companies, these individuals are shaping the tools, infrastructure, and therapies that define the future of healthcare.
Among them are executives who have led successful IPOs and acquisitions, overseen breakthrough approvals in gene and cell therapy, and helped scale technologies that accelerate drug discovery and delivery. Many have built and commercialized platforms that support not just a single treatment, but entire pipelines. Others are expanding access to care in historically underserved disease areas. Whether pioneering programmable cell therapies, launching smart manufacturing systems, or applying AI to decode disease biology, this year’s honorees stand out for their ability to translate complex science into meaningful outcomes.
This year’s awardees include Stuart Arbuckle, Chief Operating Officer of Vertex Pharmaceuticals, who is recognized for overseeing global commercial functions—including market access, patient support, supply chain, and manufacturing—for therapies addressing cystic fibrosis, sickle cell disease, and other serious conditions. Marianne De Backer, Chief Executive Officer of Vir Biotechnology, stands out for leading the company’s strategic pivot toward infectious disease and oncology, drawing on decades of experience in R&D, licensing, and global M&A at Bayer and Johnson & Johnson. Meanwhile, Dan Kagan, President and Chief Operating Officer of Scientist.com, is acknowledged for building a widely adopted research outsourcing framework that powers the company’s global marketplace, used by top pharmaceutical companies, biotech firms, and the NIH.
Awardees were selected based on their strategic and operational leadership, contributions to therapeutic innovation and platform development, and ability to advance the broader field of biotechnology and life sciences. Please join us in celebrating The Top 25 BioTech and Life Sciences Executives of 2025.
**![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/xiao-jun-ma.jpg)15. Xiao-Jun Ma  
** Company: Alamar Biosciences  
Title: Chief Technology Officer
Xiao-Jun Ma is the Chief Technology Officer of Alamar Biosciences, a privately held life sciences company developing high-sensitivity proteomics tools for early disease detection. Alamar’s platform includes its proprietary NULISA™ chemistry and the ARGO™ System, which together support automated, high-throughput protein analysis with qPCR and NGS readouts. The NULISAseq Inflammation Panel features over 200 immune and inflammatory markers and is designed for use on the ARGO System with minimal hands-on time.
Ma is a successful R&D leader with more than 20 years of experience in the life sciences and molecular diagnostics industries. Most recently he served as vice president and chief scientific officer in the Genomics Division of Bio-Techne, a pioneer in spatial genomics since its inception as Advanced Cell Diagnostics (ACD). During his 11-year tenure at ACD, Ma led the development of a world-leading portfolio of in situ RNA and DNA detection solutions for the research and clinical diagnostics markets.
Prior to joining ACD, he was vice president of R&D/biostatistics in bioTheranostics. Prior to bioTheranostics, Ma held senior bioinformatics positions at Johnson & Johnson and Monsanto/Searle (Pfizer), where he applied his multi-disciplinary knowledge in molecular biology and bioinformatics to discover novel drug targets and biomarkers. Ma received his doctorate training in biochemistry at Case Western Reserve University and the University of Iowa and post-doctoral training in molecular genetics at the University of California, Los Angeles.

## Brain-Derived Versions of Phospho-Tau Make Better Markers
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/alzforum.png)
  * August 18, 2025


###### Product:
######  Alzheimer's, Neurology
###### Topic:
###### Disease Area:
###### Sample Type:
Back to Publications​ 
  * August 18, 2025


###### Topic/Product:
######  Alzheimer's, Neurology
## Abstract
At this year’s Alzheimer’s Association International Conference, held July 27-31 in Toronto, scientists introduced a plethora of new assays for biomarkers that could improve diagnosis and tracking of AD pathology. Topping the list were immunoassays for brain-derived (BD) phospho-tau isoforms that turn up in plasma. Data hot off the bench of the lab of Jonathan Schott, University College London, indicated that these tests outperformed those for systemic p-tau fragments in identifying people who have amyloid and tau pathology. “The BD versions are just much better,” Schott told a small audience during a product presentation hosted by Alamar Biosciences, Fremont, California. Alamar now include BD p-tau isoforms in its human CNS panel. The biotech company also debuted a Nulisa panel of 123 mouse CNS proteins in Toronto. They expect this will help scientists better understand changes going on in mouse models of AD, and hence in the human brain.
The data drew praise from people in the field. “Plasma BD-tau isoforms are really important,” Henrik Zetterberg, University of Gothenburg, Mölndal, Sweden, told Alzforum. “We can finally account for peripheral nerve damage that we might see in diabetes or ALS that can drive up plasma p-tau,” he said. Gil Rabinovici, University of California, San Francisco, expressed similar sentiments. “It is very exciting to have more precise ways to measure protein from the brain rather than picking up proteins in the peripheral pool as well,” he told Alzforum. “This is such a fast-moving field. The blood-based markers are rapidly getting better.”

## Advancing Translational Research in Alzheimer’s Disease – Inside Precision Medicine
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/IPM-MASTER-LOGO-PMS-3035-1024x415-1-300x300.png)
  * August 1, 2025


###### Product:
######  Alzheimer's, Neurology
###### Topic:
###### Disease Area:
###### Sample Type:
Back to Publications​ 
  * August 1, 2025


###### Topic/Product:
######  Alzheimer's, Neurology
## Abstract
Recently Alamar Biosciences, the Alzheimer’s Disease Data Initiative (ADDI), and Gates Ventures announced a new strategic partnership aimed at creating one of the largest datasets of proteomic and clinical data for Alzheimer’s disease. The international project will profile over 40,000 plasma samples from individuals with Alzheimer’s and related dementias. This ambitious effort aims to accelerate the discovery of new biomarkers and provide deeper insights into how Alzheimer’s progresses and how it can be treated.
Damian Doherty,  _Inside Precision Medicine’_ s Editor in Chief, spoke to the CEO of Alamar Biosciences, Yuling Luo, PhD, and Niranjan Bose, PhD, Managing Director of Health & Life Sciences at Gates Ventures and interim Executive Director of the Alzheimer’s Disease Data Initiative on the importance of this collaboration and how it could transform our understanding of Alzheimer’s disease.

## TDP-43 Conference Marks Concerted Effort to Finally Snag Biomarkers – Alzforum
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/alzforum.png)
  * June 30, 2025


###### Product:
######  Alzheimer's, Neurology
###### Topic:
###### Disease Area:
###### Sample Type:
Back to Publications​ 
  * June 30, 2025


###### Topic/Product:
######  Alzheimer's, Neurology
## Abstract
The TDP-43 Summit 2025 marked a pivotal moment in the quest to develop reliable biomarkers for TDP-43, a pathological protein central to ALS and frontotemporal dementia. Scientists from across the globe gathered to share advances in imaging, fluid-based assays, and animal models—all aiming to detect and track TDP-43 pathology in living patients. A recurring theme was the urgent need for tools that can support earlier diagnosis, monitor disease progression, and evaluate therapeutic response.
Highlights included promising data from antibody-based plasma assays, emerging PET tracer efforts, and novel approaches using extracellular vesicles. While no single method has yet emerged as definitive, the field is rapidly coalescing around collaborative strategies and multi-modal detection techniques. With growing momentum and cross-sector engagement, the conference underscored a collective commitment to making TDP-43 biomarkers a clinical reality.

######  Alzheimer's, Neurology
## Abstract
Check out the latest coverage on **Alzforum** , spotlighting the NULISA™ platform and its potential to redefine diagnostics in Alzheimer’s and other neurodegenerative diseases.
From detecting attomolar concentrations of key biomarkers to streamlining multi-target analysis from small CSF and plasma volumes, NULISA is setting a new standard in fluid proteomics.
[ read full article ](https://www.alzforum.org/news/research-news/nulisa-proteomics-platform-takes-diagnostics-discovery)

## Proteomics Consortium Profiling 50K-Plus Samples From Patients With Neurodegenerative Disease
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/genome-web-logo2-300x300.png)
  * June 12, 2025


###### Product:
######  Alzheimer's, Neurology
###### Topic:
###### Disease Area:
###### Sample Type:
Back to Publications​ 
  * June 12, 2025
  * [ Adam Bonislawski ](https://www.genomeweb.com/about-us/our-staff/adam-bonislawski)


###### Topic/Product:
######  Alzheimer's, Neurology
## Abstract
NEW YORK – The Global Neurodegeneration Proteomics Consortium (GNPC) is putting together the largest set of proteomics data in neurodegenerative disease collected to date with plans to characterize roughly 50,000 plasma samples from individuals with neurodegenerative conditions.
The organization, which operates as a public-private partnership between Johnson & Johnson’s Janssen Research & Development and Gates Ventures, plans in July to release data from the first stage of the project to the broader scientific community.
That data will consist of measurements on roughly 35,000 plasma samples from roughly 25,000 individuals made using technologies including Standard BioTools’ SomaScan, Olink’s Explore HT, Alamar Biosciences’ NULISA platforms, and mass spectrometry, said Niranjan Bose, a managing director at Gates Ventures.
Gates Ventures is also working with Alamar and the Alzheimer’s Disease Data Initiative (where Bose is a member of the advisory board) to collect data on more than 40,000 plasma samples from individuals with neurodegenerative disease. Roughly 10,000 to 15,000 of those samples have or will also be run on the SomaScan 11K and Olink Explore HT platforms and will be released as part of a second GNPC dataset, Bose said. The remainder of the samples will, at least initially, be run only on the Alamar platform.

## Precision proteomics demands precision antibodies
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/nature-portifolio-09-960x720-1-300x225.jpg)
  * April 3, 2025


###### Product:
######  Alzheimer's, Neurology
###### Topic:
###### Disease Area:
###### Sample Type:
Back to Publications​ 
  * April 3, 2025


###### Topic/Product:
######  Alzheimer's, Neurology
## Abstract
Despite the hundreds of millions of vials of blood drawn every year for medical testing, scientists have only scratched the surface of its diagnostic potential. The blood proteome — which includes all proteins secreted into the blood — is a vast and largely untapped resource for markers of health or disease.
One key analytical challenge is the need to simultaneously detect multiple protein biomarkers in the blood with high sensitivity. Tod White, chief business officer at proteomics company Alamar Biosciences, likens the endeavour to trying to spot patterns of stars in the night sky.
“If you’re sitting in San Francisco, there are a lot of bright lights,” he says. “It’s very difficult to pick out the unique signals of the stars. If you remove the background light and the noise in the system, you can get much better fidelity and see the whole Milky Way.”
The method Alamar Biosciences developed to lower this signal-to-noise ratio and increase the sensitivity and specificity of protein detection in the blood is called NULISA. Similar to traditional ELISA sandwich immunoassays, it uses two highly specific antibodies that bind to two distinct epitopes in a protein biomarker.
