# NULISA™ Assays for Neurology
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/WebIcons2024_Neuron-300x300.png)
## Unlocking Neurological Diseases with   
High-Sensitivity Protein Detection
The convergence of disease modifying therapies and high-sensitivity protein detection technologies is transforming neurology. These advancements promise earlier diagnoses, personalized treatment plans, and improved patient outcomes across a spectrum of CNS diseases.
## NULISAseq Multiplex Panels
Multiplex analysis of biologically informed content with the highest-sensitivity and broadest dynamic range.
![WebIcons_CNS Panel Icon](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/WebIcons_CNS-Panel-Icon-1.png)
### NULISAseq CNS Disease Panel 120
**Profile Biomarkers of CNS Disease** at the Lowest Limit of Detection  
  
**The ONLY neurology panel with Brain-Derived Tau assays.** Simultaneous analysis of 120 proteins from a single 25ul sample with fg/ml sensitivity empowers researchers to detect disease earlier and differentiate between clinically similar phenotypes.
[ explore panel ](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/nulisaseq-cns-disease-panel/)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/WebIcons2024_Mouse-Icon.png)
### NULISAseq Mouse Panel 120
**Discover More Biology** in preclinical models   
  
With the largest multiplexed protein panel for mouse studies, researchers can comprehensively measure inflammation from precious small volume samples and maximize the information captured in basic research and preclinical studies.
[ explore panel ](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/nulisaseq-mouse-panel-120/)
## NULISAqpcr Single-plex Assays
**Ultra-high sensitivity measurement** of your most informative biomarkers.  
Detect important low abundance proteins with attomolar sensitivity (low fg/mL)
###  NEW!   
BD-pTau217 
In neurodegenerative conditions marked by Tau accumulation, protein sources may originate from either brain or peripheral tissues. For Alzheimer’s disease, when detecting pTau217 from blood or plasma it is critical to distinctly detect brain originated pTau217 versus that originated from peripheral tissues.
[ LEARN MORE ](https://alamarbio.com/nulisaqpcr-bd-ptau217-assay/)
###  NfL 
Elevated levels of Neurofilament light (NfL) can indicate the extent of neuronal injury and are useful for diagnosing and monitoring the progression of neurological diseases, such as Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), Alzheimer’s Disease (AD), Multiple Sclerosis (MS), etc.
[ REQUEST QUOTE ](https://alamarbio.com/contact-us/)
###  IL-1B 
Coming Soon! Overproduction of Interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β) is associated with various inflammatory diseases, including rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, and certain neurodegenerative disorders like Alzheimer's disease.
[ REQUEST QUOTE ](https://alamarbio.com/contact-us/)

## Advancing biomarker research for CNS Disease
  * **Precision Biomarkers for Early Diagnosis  
** Early diagnosis is key to effective intervention in CNS diseases. Biomarkers such as amyloid-β and tau proteins for Alzheimer’s Disease, α-synuclein for Parkinson’s Disease, and neurofilament light chain (NfL) for ALS, MS, and other conditions are transforming early detection capabilities. These markers enable clinicians to detect subtle pathological changes before the onset of clinical symptoms.


  * **Fluid Biomarkers from Blood and Cerebrospinal Fluid (CSF)  
** Traditionally, CSF has been the primary source for biomarker detection, but recent innovations have Blood-based biomarker detection reduces reliance on invasive procedures like lumbar punctures, improving patient compliance and accessibility. Plasma tau, NfL, and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) are emerging as reliable indicators for diseases like Alzheimer’s, FTD, and TBI, offering less invasive diagnostic options.


  * **Biomarkers for Monitoring Disease Progression  
** Dynamic biomarkers such as phosphorylated tau (p-tau) and NfL allow clinicians to track disease progression and treatment efficacy. Longitudinal tracking of biomarkers such as NfL provides valuable insights into disease progression in ALS, MS, and other neurodegenerative conditions.
  * **Improved Therapeutic Development**  
High-sensitivity detection accelerates drug development by identifying target engagement and treatment responses at early stages.


## Key Therapeutic Areas
**Alzheimer’s Disease (AD)**
Biomarkers such as amyloid-β, p-tau, and total tau (t-tau) are critical for early detection and monitoring. High-sensitivity techniques enable the detection of these markers in plasma, making routine screening feasible.
**Parkinson’s Disease (PD)**
α-synuclein aggregates in CSF and blood are being explored as diagnostic and prognostic markers. High-sensitivity assays can distinguish subtle changes associated with early disease stages.
**Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)**
NfL and other neurodegeneration-related proteins serve as reliable indicators of motor neuron injury. Their levels in blood and CSF correlate with disease progression and therapeutic response.
**Multiple Sclerosis (MS)**
NfL and GFAP are emerging as valuable biomarkers for assessing inflammatory and neurodegenerative processes in MS. High-sensitivity detection enhances the precision of these measurements.
**Frontotemporal Dementia (FTD)**
Genetic and protein biomarkers, including progranulin and tau, provide insights into FTD subtypes. Sensitive assays enable earlier differentiation from other dementias.
**Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI)**
Acute biomarkers like GFAP and ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L1 (UCH-L1) aid in diagnosing and prognosticating TBI severity. High-sensitivity detection ensures rapid and accurate evaluation in clinical settings.

## ** Detecting biomarkers in the depths of the proteome **
**Despite significant progress over the past 50 years, much of the human plasma proteome remains undetectable by existing protein analysis technologies.**
**Alamar Biosciences is a proteomics company empowering researchers to interrogate the proteome with unprecedented breadth, depth, and high-throughput precision.**
**With best-in-class attomolar sensitivity and up to 12-log dynamic range, NULISA technology enables accurate detection of highly multiplexed protein biomarkers from a 25 µl liquid biopsy specimen.**
**Translational scientists can seamlessly and confidently transition across their biomarker discovery and validation journey using the same platform. New insights from large cohorts and population studies will revolutionize our understanding of the human proteome and unlock its full potential for improving human health.**
**![NULISA Limit of Detection](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/Charts_Generic_2024_LOD-Large.png)**
## ** Accelerating biomarker development **
**Clinically relevant biomarkers that enable earlier disease diagnosis and personalized medicine require ultra-high sensitivity. NULISA breaks through the current detection limits by dramatically reducing the background noise often inherent to multiplex assay technologies. With unprecedented sensitivity, high multiplexing, and a fully automated workflow, NULISA expedites the discovery, profiling, and validation of clinically relevant, translatable protein biomarkers across the therapeutic development pipeline.**
**Alamar Biosciences’ mission is to enable the earliest detection of disease by advancing precision proteomics. As a leading proteomics company, we provide cutting-edge solutions that empower researchers from academic institutions, core labs, biopharmaceutical, and biotech companies to push the boundaries of protein research. Our innovative approaches to proteomics analysis will accelerate your product development, enhance precision, and unlock groundbreaking discoveries.**

# NULISAseq™ Mouse Panel 120
## Most comprehensive coverage of protein expression in murine models
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/WebIcons2024_Mouse-Icon-1-300x300.png)Encompassing 120 proteins selected for their importance in biomedical research, the NULISAseq Mouse Panel 120 targets key pathways involved in inflammation, neurodegeneration and oncogenesis. By leveraging advanced multiplexing technology, the NULISAseq Mouse Panel 120 provides researchers with a high sensitivity and high throughput method for elucidating complex biological mechanisms and identifying potential therapeutic targets. Whether investigating disease pathophysiology or evaluating the efficacy of novel interventions in pre-clinical models, this robust panel offers unparalleled depth and precision in protein expression profiling.

Attomolar (fg/ml)

## NULISAseq™ Mouse Panel 120
### Most comprehensive coverage of protein expression in murine models
Biomarkers of disease progression and therapeutic response are transforming the field of Neurology. Developed in collaboration with leading neuroscience researchers, the NULISASeq™ CNS Disease Panel 120 enables ultra-sensitive, multiplexed quantification of 120+ neuro-specific and inflammatory proteins from just 10 µL of plasma or CSF.
By leveraging advanced multiplexing technology, the NULISAseq Mouse Panel 120 provides researchers with a high sensitivity and high throughput method for elucidating complex biological mechanisms and identifying potential therapeutic targets. Whether investigating disease pathophysiology or evaluating the efficacy of novel interventions in pre-clinical models, this robust panel offers unparalleled depth and precision in protein expression profiling.

## Alamar Biosciences & University of Oxford Inflammation Grant Program
### APPLICATIONS NOW CLOSED
## You've seen the data. Now generate your own. Apply for your chance to run your samples with the NULISAseq™ Inflammation Panel 250
The University of Oxford, in partnership with Alamar Biosciences, is pleased to announce a targeted funding initiative to support high-impact translational immunology research.
This programme will support three selected projects with subsidised access to the [**NULISAseq**](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/nulisa-inflammation-panel/)™ [**Inflammation Panel 250**](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/nulisa-inflammation-panel/), delivered via the **University of Oxford Multiomics Platforms Facility**.
The panel enables ultra-sensitive, multiplexed quantification of low-abundance cytokines, chemokines, and immune mediators – unlocking biological insights not accessible with conventional approaches.
**This initiative aims to:**
  * Enable generation of high-resolution immune datasets
  * Support pilot data for larger funding applications
  * Accelerate translation from discovery to clinical insight
  * Strengthen Oxford’s leadership in high-throughput immune profiling and multiomics


**We welcome applications across the Oxford research community, including:**
  * Women’s health (e.g. endometriosis, reproductive immunology)
  * Cardiovascular disease (e.g. myocardial infarction, vascular inflammation)
  * Autoimmune and inflammatory disorders
  * Infectious disease and host response
  * Neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration


We particularly encourage proposals with **clear translational potential** , especially those aligned with **well-characterised cohorts** or that could scale into larger studies.
Do you have questions? Please reach out to tburley@alamarbio.com.

– Be 18 years of age or older at the time of application.
Members of the immediate families of Alamar Biosciences employees and directors, and persons living in the same household as such individuals, are ineligible to apply.
**Award Details:**
– 3 awards are available.  
– Each award consists of one [NULISAseq™ Inflammation Panel 250](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/nulisa-inflammation-panel/) per project (up to 86 samples).  
– Analysis will be performed by the Oxford Multiomics Platforms Facility.  
– Analysis must commence within six (6) weeks of award notification. Extensions may be granted at Alamar’s sole discretion upon written request.
**Cost Structure:**
This programme is heavily subsidised. The Inflammation 250 panels have been internally validated and confirmed to perform within expected specifications; accordingly, no cost is attributed to the panels themselves.
Successful applicants will be required to cover the following costs only:  
– £3,000 per plate (sequencing costs)  
– Associated service fees from the Oxford Multiomics Platforms Facility, charged at cost.
_Applicants are encouraged to confirm that institutional budget availability for these costs is in place prior to submitting an application._
**Award Selection Criteria:**
– Sample matrix: No restriction (e.g. plasma, serum, CSF, tissue, or other).  
– Applications will be jointly reviewed by the University of Oxford and Alamar Biosciences.  
– Grant submissions must be received by 11:59 PM British Summer Time on Friday, 01 May 2026.
**Award Details:**
Successful applicants will be notified by email no later than Friday, 15 May 2026. All applicants will receive confirmation that their submission was received.
**Publication of Results:**
All grant submissions are confidential to the individual submitter and will not be published or distributed to third parties.
Upon project completion, each grant recipient agrees to participate in one of the following activities relating to the specific project, within 12 months of project completion, with details to be mutually agreed in good faith between Alamar and the recipient:

metadata.og:description: NULISAqpcr™ NfL Assay From Injury to Insight. Achieve higher precision of NfL detection across disease types Neurofilament light (NfL) is a structural protein in neurons that supports axons and aids transport. When axons are damaged, NfL is released into CSF and blood. Elevated NfL levels indicate neuronal injury and serve as a biomarker for diagnosing […]

## NULISAqpcr™ NfL Assay
### From Injury to Insight.
##### Achieve higher precision of NfL detection across disease types
Neurofilament light (NfL) is a structural protein in neurons that supports axons and aids transport. When axons are damaged, NfL is released into CSF and blood. Elevated NfL levels indicate neuronal injury and serve as a biomarker for diagnosing and monitoring neurological diseases such as Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis, Alzheimer’s Disease, Parkinson’s Disease, Multiple Sclerosis, Traumatic Brain Injury and stroke.
The NULISAqpcr™ NfL Assay delivers precise detection of neurofilament light protein in serum or plasma using just 10 µL* of sample. Its analytical performance is rigorously validated, ensuring exceptional accuracy and confidence in every result.
_*Sample input volumes vary. Please see product manual for details._
[ Request a Quote ](https://alamarbio.com/contact-us/)
### Quantify More with fg/mL Sensitivity
##### A 7-point standard curve enables absolute quantitation of NfL.

## Biomarkers for Parkinson's Disease  
Research Grant Program
### THE GRANT IS NOW CLOSED. THANK YOU FOR YOUR SUBMISSIONS!
## Do you have a research project that would benefit from comprehensive high sensitivity analysis of protein biomarkers in blood?
**The Parkinson’s Disease Grant Program will award three (3) research projects with analysis of 86 samples using the NULISAseq ™ Neuro 220 Panel through Alamar’s Technology Access Program. **
The **NULISAseq ™ Neuro 220 Panel** offers comprehensive coverage of the Hallmarks of Neurodegenerative disease with highly sensitive and specific multiplexed analysis of 220 biomarkers from biofluids, including **25 new biomarkers associated with Parkinson’s Disease,** 15 of which were developed with support from **The Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson’s Research,** providing researchers with an automated solution to dissect heterogeneity and identify signatures of disease initiation and progression in clinical cohorts.
  * **Biomarker Discovery:** Identify novel biomarkers associated with Parkinson’s Disease by measuring a wide range of proteins simultaneously in different disease states and compare them to healthy controls. 
  * **Drug Development and Clinical Trials:** Evaluate the effects of potential therapeutic agents on specific protein targets related to inflammation and assess their efficacy in preclinical and clinical studies.
  * **Diagnostic Development:** Measure specific protein markers known to be associated with the presence and severity of diseases and differentiate between different subtypes or stages of a particular disease. 


![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Brain_FINAL_Alpha_WebHome-2.png)
**Terms and Conditions**
**Award Selection Criteria:**
  * Access to banked samples with associated clinical annotations 
  * Ability to complete project within a 6-month period 
  * Potential to publish the results on high impact factors as determined by the judges 
  * Grant submissions must be received by 11:59 PM Pacific Time on Monday, May 4, 2026. 


**Publication of Results:**   
All grant submissions are confidential to the individual submitter and will not be published or distributed. Upon project completion, the grant winner agrees to participate in one of the following activities relating to the specific project, with specific details of the applicable activity to be mutually agreed upon in good faith by Alamar and the winner: local seminar, webinar, case study, blog post, or poster presentation. Each winner agrees that Alamar shall have the right to use de-identified data from the winner’s project in application notes or marketing literature.
**Eligibility and Requirements:  
** In order to be eligible to win the grant of the NULISAseq™ Neuro Panel 220, applicants must be actively enrolled at an academic institution or employed at a research facility in a capacity in which they are able to perform research on and have capabilities to collect samples as well as run their project as described in the submitted abstract. The grant winner must be age 18 or older. Members of the immediate families of Alamar employees and directors, and persons living in the same household as such persons, are ineligible for this grant. 
**Miscellaneous:  
** Alamar Biosciences, Inc. is the sponsor of this grant. No purchase is necessary to enter. By applying for the grant, each applicant agrees to these terms and conditions and that Alamar may process the personal data he or she provides in accordance with Alamar’s privacy policies available at Alamarbio.com/privacy. The grant winner or its applicable institution is responsible for any tax liability incurred by accepting the services provided. This is not a “cash in hand” grant and the grant winner has no option to receive any cash payment or alternative award in lieu of the offered services. The grant may not be transferred or assigned. The services, if any, will be provided subject to Alamar’s standard terms and conditions related to TAP service projects, as the same may be amended from time to time. Alamar has not made any warranty, representation, or guarantee, express or implied, with respect to the grant, including, without limitation, the provided service’s quality or fitness for a particular purpose. Alamar reserves the right in its sole discretion to cancel, modify or suspend the grant program. ## Data Analysis Solutions
### Streamline time to result with our integrated analysis solutions
Integrated software solutions supporting run setup, QC, analysis, and biological insight generation across cloud and on-prem deployments.
**ARGO Command Center**
  * Quickly set up and queue runs on the ARGO™ HT System
  * Monitor run status remotely through cloud-connected access
  * Manage users and groups with role-based access control
  * Automate QC and analysis of your runs & Samples


**NULISA Analysis Software**
  * Perform QC and data normalization for multiplex panels
  * Combine data across runs into a unified analysis
  * Conduct advanced statistical analysis to uncover biological insights
  * Generate publication-ready charts and visualizations

### Precision Proteomics for Cancer and Immuno-Oncology Research
Oncology and immunology are converging in powerful ways, as researchers uncover the immune system’s role in tumor progression, response to therapy, and adverse events.
Whether profiling cytokines, monitoring response to immunotherapy or identifying markers of toxicity, NULIS assays offer ultra-sensitive multiplexed assays that enable researchers to detect and quantify critical biomarkers in clinical cohorts.
### Key Applications in Oncology
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/icon-early-detection.svg)
#### Early Detection
Protein biomarkers enable early cancer detection, often before symptoms appear, improving the chances of successful treatment
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/icon-personalized-medicine.svg)
#### Personalized Medicine
Biomarker profiling helps tailor treatment strategies to individual patients based on their specific cancer type and protein expression patterns.
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/icon-monitoring-disease-progression.svg)
#### Monitoring Disease Progression
Protein biomarkers can track cancer progression and response to therapy, allowing for timely adjustments in treatment plans.
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/icon-risk-of-adverse-events.svg)
#### Risk of Adverse Events
Immuno-profiling has identified early signatures associated with several adverse immune reactions to IO therapy.
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/icon-minimally-invasive-testing.svg)
#### Minimally Invasive Testing
Many protein biomarkers can be detected in blood, urine, or other body fluids, reducing the need for invasive biopsies.

## Technology Access Program (TAP)
### Experience industry leading sensitivity and access to pre-commercial technology
Alamar’s Technology Access Program provides researchers an opportunity to experience the ultra-high sensitivity of both NULISA™ [panels and assays](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/) to get proof-of-concept data in your sample cohort before purchasing the [ARGO™ HT System](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/argo-system/).
### How it works
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Frame-332-1.png)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Frame-391-7.png)
### TAP Services
#### Pro Services
Full service analysis for commercially available panels and assays
  * Consultation of experimental design
  * Sample analysis including sequencing
  * Bioinformatics support Data Analysis of up to 40 hrs
  * Provide final data report and data analysis review with our professional services team.


#### Custom Assay Development
Full service custom assay development
  * Consultation of experimental design
  * Sourcing, evaluation and selection of best performing antibody pairs
  * Optimization and validation of assay performance
  * Provide final report and data analysis review


### Contact Us
###### FOR RESEARCH USE ONLY. Not for use in diagnostic procedures.

## NULISAqpcr™ Custom Assay Development
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/nulisa-qpcr.svg)
### Harness the Sensitivity of NULISA for Custom Biomarker Assays
The NULISAqpcr™ Custom Assay Development Kit provides researchers with a flexible solution for creating targeted biomarker assays with high sensitivity and precision. Ideal for applications requiring highly specific and reproducible data, this customizable kit allows scientists to use their own antibodies to create assays tailored to their individual research.
[ Request a Quote ](https://alamarbio.com/contact-us/)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/DropGrid_Texture_WhiteFlatUneven-copy-3.svg)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/DropGrid_Texture_WhiteFlatUneven-copy-4.svg)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/icon-unmatched-sensitivity-1.svg)
Ultra-High Sensitivity
Detect ultra-low abundant targets with attomolar (fg/mL) precision
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/icon-minimal-input-required-1-1.svg)
Minimal Input Required
Cost effective with only 100 µg input per antibody target
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/icon-multi-target-detection-1.svg)
Multi-target Detection
Flexibility to conjugate up to 4 pairs of antibodies.
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/icon-expert-assay-development-support-1.svg)
Expert Assay Development Support
From initial design to final implementation
### Fully customizable, high-sensitivity proteomics
Create a unique NULISAqpcr™ assay in 6 steps and with the power of the [ARGO™ HT System.](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/argo-system/)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Frame-331.png)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Frame-391-1.png)

## NULISA™ Dried Blood Spot Extraction Kit
### From Spot to Signal. Standardize proteomics from microsamples.
The NULISA™ DBS Extraction Kit provides a standardized, high-throughput workflow for recovering protein analytes from dried blood and dried plasma spots. Combined with NULISA’s attomolar sensitivity, the kit unlocks high-quality multiplexed proteomic data from minimally invasive, remotely collected samples.
### Built for High-Quality Multiplexed Data
  * **85–95%** target detectability across NULISAseq panels on most devices tested.
  * **96-sample** filter-plate format for high-throughput processing.
  * **4+** validated microsampling devices with a device-agnostic protocol.


![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/DBS-TN_Finger-Mitra-Lrg.png)
[ Request a Quote ](https://alamarbio.com/contact-us/)
Standardized Extraction Workflow
A validated, ready-to-use reagent kit with buffer, filter plates, collection plates, and plate seals.
Device-Agnostic Compatibility
One workflow, multiple device options. Optimized across leading microsampling   
devices including Capitainer, Telimmune, Mitra, and Tasso. 
High-Throughput Format
96-well filter-plate format scales to large population health, clinical, and translational research studies.
High Detectability from Microsamples
85-95% target detectability across CNS and Inflammation panels on most devices tested.
Enables Remote and Longitudinal Designs
Supports ambient-shipped, minimally invasive samples. Reaches populations and settings where traditional venipuncture is not feasible.
Built for the NULISA Platform
Pairs the kit’s standardized extraction with NULISA’s attomolar sensitivity for multiplexed protein measurement from a single small-volume sample.
### Device-agnostic
### Compatible with Leading Microsampling Devices
One extraction workflow, validated across the devices your studies already use.
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/DBS-TN_Device-CapB.png)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/DBS-TN_Device-CapSEPT10.png)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/DBS-TN_Device-Mitra.png)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/DBS-TN_Device-TASSO.png)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/DBS-TN_Device-Telimmune.png)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/DBS-TN_Device-Whatman.png)
Simple. Repeatable. scalable.
### The DBS Extraction Workflow
Five steps from microsample to NULISA-ready extract. The filter-plate format is built for routine 96-well processing.
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/DBS-Step1-2.png)
### Step 1
Take the dried blood spot discs (Telimmune, Capitainer, or other collection devices) and transfer them onto a 96-well filter plate.
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/DBS-Step2-2.png)
### Step 2
Stack the collection plate below the extraction filter plate and secure with lab tape.
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/DBS-Step3-2.png)
### Step 3
Add NULISA DBS Extraction Buffer.
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/DBS-Step4-2.png)
### Step 4
Seal the plate and agitate the filter plate stack and centrifuge.
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/DBS-Step5-1.png)
### Step 5
Collect the samples in the collection plate and store until ready to be tested.
[ Request a Quote ](https://alamarbio.com/contact-us/)
## Where it fits
### Studies and Settings Where DBS Changes What's Possible
**Longitudinal and At-Home Studies  
** Frequent self-collection from a fingerstick. Capture biomarker dynamics over time without burdening participants.
**Translational and Clinical Research  
** Standardized sample prep means reproducible data across sites. Scale studies without sacrificing assay performance.
**Pediatric and Vulnerable Populations  
** Minimally invasive collection opens access to populations where venipuncture is impractical.
**Global and Remote Cohorts  
** Ambient-stable samples remove the cold chain. Study geographies that were previously out of reach.
**Discovery and Biomarker Programs  
** Pair the kit with NULISA CNS, Neuro 220, and Inflammation panels for multiplexed protein measurement at attomolar sensitivity.

## NULISAqpcr AD 5-plex Assay
### One Panel, 5 Key Biomarkers
The **NULISAqpcr AD 5-plex Assay** integrates biomarkers across the ATNI framework – Amyloid (A), Tau (T), and Neurodegeneration (N) and Inflammation (I) to enable earlier detection, resolution of disease heterogeneity, and better prediction of therapeutic outcomes in Alzheimer’s Disease research. 
The AD 5-plex assay provides the possibility of an integrated understanding of Alzheimer’s pathology with simultaneous quantitative measurement of five key biomarkers – **BD-pTau217, NfL, Aβ42, GFAP, and APOE4** carrier status – from a single, non-invasive blood or plasma sample. 
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/AD-Neuron-01-1024x579.png)
### Key Features and Benefits
Precision Proteomics
Only multiplexed panel to combine the sensitivity and specificity necessary to integrate protein markers and carrier status assessment for a complete picture of Alzheimer’s pathology.
Integrated analysis from minimal sample input
Simultaneous measurement of BD-pTau217, Aβ42, NfL, and GFAP and APOE4 from a single 35µL sample.
Non-Invasive Sample
Obtain robust results from standard blood draws, streamlining collection and processing.
Automated Workflow
Efficiently analyse up to 252 samples in just 8 hours with less than 30-min of hands-on time for laboratory staff.
### Transforming Alzheimer’s Research with Precision Proteomics
Alamar Biosciences is dedicated to redefining risk and progression monitoring in neurodegenerative diseases. By moving beyond single-analyte testing, NULISAqpcr AD 5-Plex Assay provides a multidimensional profile to support a more accurate interpretation of Alzheimer’s disesase biology. 
### The NULISA AD 5-plex Assay includes: ​
  * #### BD-pTau217:
BD-pTau217 is a highly specific indicator of amyloid and tau protein abnormalities in the brain. Its elevated levels reflect the presence of amyloid plaque and tau tangles, which are the defining features of Alzheimer’s disease pathology. By detecting BD-pTau217 in blood, clinicians and researchers can monitor the progression of neurofibrillary degeneration non-invasively, making it a powerful tool for early detection and tracking disease dynamics over time.
  * #### Aβ42 (Amyloid-beta 42):
A core neuropathological hallmark of Alzheimer’s disease, reflecting amyloid-β biology associated with plaque deposition. Reduced levels of Aβ42 in blood or cerebrospinal fluid are associated with increased amyloid deposition in the brain, a key step in the disease’s development. Tracking Aβ42 provides insight into amyloid pathology and is essential for understanding disease stage, progression, and response to amyloid-targeting therapies.
  * #### GFAP (Glial fibrillary acidic protein):
Elevated GFAP levels indicate astroglial activation, which often accompanies and amplifies neuroinflammatory processes in Alzheimer’s and related disorders. By measuring GFAP, researchers gain valuable information about the brain’s immune response and the extent of glial involvement in neurodegeneration.


  * #### NfL (Neurofilament light chain):
NfL is released into the blood when neurons are damaged or undergoing degeneration. As a sensitive marker of axonal injury, increased NfL levels signal active neurodegeneration, not only in Alzheimer’s disease but also in a range of other neurodegenerative disorders. Measuring NfL allows for the assessment of ongoing neuronal damage, making it valuable for disease monitoring and evaluating therapeutic interventions.


  * #### APOE4 carrier status:
The APOE4 genetic variant is the strongest known inherited risk factor for late-onset Alzheimer’s disease with important implications for disease trajectory and therapeutic risk, including amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA). Determining APOE4 status helps stratify risk, personalise monitoring strategies, and inform decisions about prevention and intervention.


### Designed to deliver a new standard of precision
The NULISAqpcr AD 5-plex Assay enables researchers to develop the next generation of testing:
Earlier identification of AD relevant biology
Improved biological staging across the AD continuum
Longitudinal monitoring of disease progression and therapeutic response
Enhanced screening and enrichment of clinical trial participants
Scalable deployment beyond specialized research centers
Experience NULISAqpcr AD 5-plex Assay through our Technology Access Program (TAP).

## NULISAseq™ Inflammation Panel AQ
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/graphic-inflammation-aq-wheel-01.png)
### Quantitate More Immune Biomarkers   
in your clinical cohort studies
Compare the relative quantities for over 250 proteins while generating absolute quantitative values for >150 biomarkers – all with a single comprehensive tool for measuring inflammation longitudinally and across clinical research studies.
Offering unparalleled coverage of the immune system, the NULISAseq Inflammation Panel AQ enables the discovery of novel signatures across 250 targets while delivering precise absolute quantitative measurements for over 150 key biomarkers. With exceptional fg/mL sensitivity to detect biomarker levels in both normal, baseline, and disease samples, the NULISAseq Inflammation Panel AQ empowers researchers to track changes in key proteins essential in biomarker discovery and drug development, including pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic and toxicology studies or after therapeutic treatments in clinical cohorts.
[ Request a Quote ](https://alamarbio.com/contact-us/)
Absolute Quantitation
250+ biomarkers with absolute quantitation for 150+ targets
Attomolar Sensitivity
Ultra-high sensitivity (fg/mL) to detect low abundant targets
12 logs Dynamic Range
Measure a spectrum of biological expression levels
Highly Reproducible
Median CVs <10%
### NULISA Immunology Grant Program

Apply for the **NULISA Immunology Grant Program** for a chance to experience the NULISAseq Immune 340 Panel for your immune-related research.

## NULISAqpcr™ Single-Plex Assays
### Ultra-high sensitivity measurement of your most informative biomarkers.
NULISAqpcr™ Single-plex assays deliver ultra-sensitive, attomolar-level protein quantification with exceptional reproducibility (CV <10%) and over 7 logs of dynamic range. Designed for researchers seeking precision and efficiency, these assays enable high-throughput, single-target analysis on the ARGO™ HT system—without the need for additional instrumentation.
Whether you’re validating biomarkers or exploring low-abundance targets, NULISAqpcr™ empowers confident decision-making with minimal sample input and rapid turnaround. Accelerate your discovery with the power of NULISA’s nucleic acid-linked immunoassay technology

## NULISAseq™ Immune 340 Panel
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Immune340-01.png)
### Broad enough to discover. Sensitive enough to trust.
Immune biology doesn’t work in isolation. Every immune response is shaped by the interaction of dozens of pathways and profiling one pathway at a time may miss important biology. The NULISAseq™ Immune 340 Panel spans innate and adaptive immunity with simultaneous measurement of checkpoint biology, immune regulation, cytokines, chemokines, regulation, complement and cell-death pathways. With attomolar sensitivity and broad dynamic range, it resolves low-abundance mediators alongside high-abundance ones — delivering comprehensive immune profiling from a single sample.

## NULISAseq™ Inflammation Panel 250
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/graphic-inflammation-panel-250-1.svg)
### Deepest Profiling of Inflammatory Response
NULISAseq™ Inflammation Panel 250 provides the most comprehensive coverage of immune response with unprecedented sensitivity to detect baseline levels of low abundant cytokines.
Reliably discover and validate inflammatory biomarkers across diverse disease states with Alamar Biosciences’ NULISAseq™ Inflammation Panel 250. Based on our proprietary NULISA™ technology, this inflammatory response panel reports unparalleled accuracy on 250 of the most relevant and low-abundance inflammation targets in biofluids.
Enable the early detection of disease signatures across autoimmune, neuroinflammatory, and immune-oncology research studies with the NULISAseq Inflammation Panel 250.

12 logs Dynamic Range

# Neurodegenerative Disease Biomarker Detection Using an Ultra-Sensitive Profiling Method
## Webinar
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://www.workcast.com/register?cpak=3018982020663234)
## Neurodegenerative Disease Biomarker Detection Using an Ultra-Sensitive Profiling Method
#### Featuring:
#### **![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/HenrikZetterbergHS-150x150.png)Henrik Zetterberg, MD, PhD**
##### Professor of Neurochemistry  
University of Gothenburg
#### **![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/DougHinerfeld-150x150.png)Doug Hinerfeld, PhD**
##### Senior Director of Application Support  
Alamar Biosciences
Brain-derived biomarkers of neurodegenerative diseases are important targets for new therapies. In the context of Alzheimer’s disease, scientists are exploring the use of protein biomarkers for early diagnosis, screening, prognosis prediction, and disease monitoring. But these markers are often present at very low concentrations in plasma or serum, much too low for most existing proteomics assays to detect and measure.
In this GEN webinar, Henrik Zetterberg, MD, PhD, an expert in Alzheimer’s disease, will discuss his efforts to discover and validate blood-based biomarkers for various CNS disorders. During his presentation, he will share data from his evaluation of the NULISA immunoassay platform’s ability to detect biomarkers of Alzheimer’s disease from serum. You will also hear from Doug Hinerfeld, PhD, who will discuss the NULISA platform’s multiplex and protein marker detection capabilities in more depth.
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/GENlogo_ColorBackground_062618-300x53.webp)

## Alamar Certified Service Providers
### Alamar Biosciences is dedicated to ensuring access to innovative technologies.
Alamar Certified Service Providers (CSPs) are trusted partners selected for their deep technical expertise and proven excellence in delivering high-quality proteomics services using Alamar’s NULISAseq™ platform and ARGO™ systems. As an extension of the Alamar ecosystem, CSPs enable researchers and biopharma teams to accelerate discovery and translation with ultra-sensitive, highly multiplexed protein measurements—without the need to build in-house capabilities. From study design and assay execution to data generation and interpretation, Alamar CSPs provide reliable, scalable, and standardized services to help transform complex biological questions into actionable insights.

### Unlocking The Proteome
## NULISATM Technology
The NULISA™ Platform sets a new standard in proteomic analysis with attomolar sensitivity and high multiplexing, allowing for unprecedented biomarker detection and quantitation.
By leveraging a proprietary sequential immunocomplex capture and release mechanism and the latest advances in Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS), the NULISA technology provides both ultra-high sensitivity and scalable multiplexing.
[ Watch full video ](https://alamarbio.com/technology/nulisa-platform/)
×
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/NatureComms-2.png)
Publication 
###  NULISA: a novel proteomic liquid biopsy platform with attomolar sensitivity and high multiplexing
[ Read the publication ](https://alamarbio.com/publication/nulisa-a-novel-proteomic-liquid-biopsy-platform-with-attomolar-sensitivity-and-high-multiplexing/)
### Benefits Of NULISA
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Group-162.png)
Ultra High Sensitivity
* * *
###  Detect what matters most, in the samples that most matter
Attomolar sensitivity for detection and baseline quantitation of critical biomarkers from non-invasive sample types as well as remote sampling devices.
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Group-163.png)
High Specificity
* * *
###  Distinguish between isoforms and PTMs
Assays developed to detect individual isoforms and a variety of post-translational modifications. Antibodies are selected for reduced cross reactivity with known homologs.
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Group-164.png)
Scalable Multiplex
* * *
###  Discover and validate on one platform
Flexible, scalable chemistry provides the ability to focus in on a single target, or multiplex hundreds to potentially thousands of targets in a single sample on one platform.
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Group-165.png)
Broad Dynamic Range
* * *
###  Measure Changes Across the Biological Spectrum
With single plex up to 7 logs and multiplex up to 12 logs of dynamic range, NULISA enables quantitation across a broad range of biological expression levels without the need for dilution.
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Group-166.png)
Automation
* * *
###  Generate reproducible data quickly with minimal effort 
Fully automated workflow with <30 minutes of total hands-on time, can processes up to 288 samples per run batch.
### The Biomarker Edge
![Ep.5: Oxford's Prof. John Todd on the Revolution Powering Precision Medicine](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Episode5-prof.john_.png)
### Ep.5: Oxford's Prof. John Todd on the Revolution Powering Precision Medicine
Prof. John Todd, Professor of Precision Medicine at the University of Oxford's Nuffield Department of Medicine, explains why enabling technologies — from PCR to today's proteomics platforms — drive scientific discovery, and why Alamar Bioscience's NULISA assay (including its Argo platform and CNS panel) has become central to his lab's work in type 1 diabetes, neuroinflammation, and biomarker-driven medicine.
![Ep. 4: Oxford's Prof. John Todd discusses NULISA for Type 1 Diabetes Research](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Episode4-prof.john_.png)
### Ep. 4: Oxford's Prof. John Todd discusses NULISA for Type 1 Diabetes Research
Prof. John Todd, Professor of Precision Medicine at the University of Oxford's Nuffield Department of Medicine, explains why his lab at the Centre for Human Genetics added Alamar Bioscience's NULISA assay and Argo platform to its proteomics toolkit — and what it revealed about interleukin-2 (IL-2) therapy in type 1 diabetes.
![Ep. 3: Dr. Cheryl Wellington on Fluid Biomarkers in Alzheimer’s, TBI, and Stroke](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Episode_3.jpg)
### Ep. 3: Dr. Cheryl Wellington on Fluid Biomarkers in Alzheimer’s, TBI, and Stroke
In this third episode of The Biomarker Edge, Dr. Cheryl Wellington from the University of British Columbia, discusses her work advancing fluid biomarkers in Alzheimer’s disease, traumatic brain injury, and stroke. She shares insights on launching a new biomarker core facility, building collaborations with over 120 clinical partners, and expanding biomarker applications from pediatric to geriatric care. Dr. Wellington highlights how ultra-sensitive, multiplexed technologies like ARGO™ and NULISA™ are enabling low-volume specimen analysis, broad biomarker panels, and translational research that bridges clinical and pre-clinical models.
![Ep. 2: Dr. Nicholas Ashton on Blood-Based Biomarkers in Alzheimer's Disease](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Episode_2.jpg)
### Ep. 2: Dr. Nicholas Ashton on Blood-Based Biomarkers in Alzheimer's Disease
In this episode of The Biomarker Edge series, Dr. Nicholas Ashton from Banner Health explores the clinical utility of emerging plasma biomarkers—including p-tau217, NfL, GFAP, and others—in Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias. He discusses how high-sensitivity, multiplex platforms like NULISA™ are enabling researchers to detect low-abundance CNS proteins in blood with greater precision than ever before.
![Ep 1: Dr. Henrik Zetterberg on Fluid Biomarkers in Neurodegenerative Disease](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Episode_1.jpg)
### Ep 1: Dr. Henrik Zetterberg on Fluid Biomarkers in Neurodegenerative Disease
In this premiere episode of The Biomarker Edge, world-renowned neurologist and biomarker expert Dr. Henrik Zetterberg discusses the urgent need for ultra-sensitive, multiplexed fluid biomarker assays to advance neurodegenerative disease research.

## NULISAseq™ Neuro 220   
Pilot Program
## What could you uncover with a more complete view of neurodegenerative disease biology?
Researchers in Australia and New Zealand affiliated with an academic institution, hospital, biotech, biopharma or research organization are invited to apply for Neuro 220 Panel analysis performed by Geneworks Pty Ltd. **Applications open 16 September 2026 and close 11:59 PM AEST on 30 September 2026 (2:59 AM NZDT, 1 October).** Eligibility criteria and the Terms and Conditions below apply.
Two (2) research projects will each be awarded analysis of up to 43 samples using the Neuro 220 Panel (a full kit processes 86 samples), providing deep insight into the biological mechanisms underlying neurological disease.
The Neuro 220 Panel measures 220 protein biomarkers from a single sample with ultra-high sensitivity, supporting research across Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, ALS/motor neuron disease, traumatic brain injury, multiple sclerosis, gliomas, and other neurological disorders.
For ALS/MND research, Neuro 220 gives a systems-level view of disease biology across protein aggregation and proteostasis, neuronal injury, inflammation, and synaptic function — which may help identify molecular subtypes and co-pathologies for patient stratification, and support biomarker-driven therapeutic development across pathways including SOD1, TDP-43 (TARDBP), STMN2, and NfL and NEFH.
The panel also features:
  * 13 tau assays, including eMTBR-Tau, a marker associated with tau tangle burden
  * 25 Parkinson’s disease biomarkers developed with support from The Michael J. Fox Foundation
  * Detection of low-abundance biomarkers in plasma or CSF
  * Automated workflows for high reproducibility and scalability


Recipients cover sample shipping (including customs, duties, and any biosecurity import permits), are expected to complete the project within six (6) months of data delivery, and agree to one dissemination activity (seminar, webinar, blog post, case study, or poster) within twelve (12) months of completion.  

**Apply by September 30 , 2026:**
![Neurological-Disorders](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/AlamarBiosciencesInc-329942-Treating-Neurological-Disorders-blogbanner2_2500x2500.png)
**Terms and Conditions**
**1. Sponsor and Acceptance**
Alamar Biosciences, Inc., 47071 Bayside Parkway, Fremont, California 94538, USA (“Alamar”) and Geneworks Pty Ltd (ABN [61 070 039 913]), 28 Dalgleish Street, Thebarton, SA 5031, Australia (“Geneworks”) are the sponsors of the NULISAseq™ Neuro 220 Pilot Program (the “Program”). No purchase or payment is necessary. Awards are made on scientific merit as assessed by the judges, not by chance.
By submitting an application, each applicant (“Applicant”) agrees to these Terms and Conditions (these “Terms”) and to the decisions of Alamar, Geneworks and their judges, which are final and binding on matters of eligibility and selection. Any additional Program details published at alamarbio.com or by Geneworks form part of these Terms.
These Terms incorporate the Alamar Grant Programs Terms and Conditions at alamarbio.com/grant-program-terms-and-conditions/ (the “General Grant Terms”). For this Program, each reference to “Alamar” in the General Grant Terms includes Geneworks, each acting severally. These Terms prevail to the extent of any inconsistency.
**2. Eligibility**
An Applicant must be at least 18 years of age and must be actively enrolled at, or employed in a research capacity by, an academic institution, hospital, biotech, biopharma or other research organization. An Applicant must have access to samples suitable for the proposed project, together with the rights and approvals necessary to provide them to Geneworks, and must have or reasonably expect to obtain institutional authorization to accept an Award.
Employees, officers, directors, and contractors of Alamar, Geneworks and their respective affiliates, members of their immediate families, and persons living in the same household as any such individual are not eligible.
The Program is not open where prohibited or restricted by law. Neither Alamar nor Geneworks will make an Award to any person or entity located in, or subject to the jurisdiction of, a country or region subject to comprehensive U.S. economic sanctions, or identified on a U.S., Australian, or New Zealand restricted-party or sanctions list.
**3. The Award**
Each award of Panel analysis services made under the Program is an “Award,” and the person to whom an Award is made is a “Recipient.”
Number of Awards: 2.
Each Award consists of analysis of up to 43 samples using the NULISAseq™ Neuro 220 Panel, performed by Geneworks. Alamar and Geneworks may adjust the number of samples in an Award to suit the 86-sample kit configuration.
Accepted sample types: human plasma, serum, or cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)
Alamar and Geneworks cover the standard Neuro 220 Panel analysis service and standard bioinformatics report. The Recipient covers sample collection, shipping (including customs, duties, and any biosecurity or import permits), and any additional bioinformatics services beyond that report. Neither Alamar nor Geneworks is responsible for samples damaged, degraded, or lost in transit.
An Award is not a cash grant and may not be exchanged for cash or an alternative award. Its approximate value is A$22,323.50. An Award is personal to the Recipient and may not be transferred or assigned, except that Alamar and Geneworks may permit it to be administered by the Recipient’s institution. Alamar and Geneworks may make fewer Awards than stated, or none, if in their judgment an insufficient number of applications meet the selection criteria.
**4. How to Apply, Selection, and Timeline**
Applications must be submitted using the form on the Program page at alamarbio.com and must include a project abstract, sample cohort summary, proposed timeline, and institutional affiliation. The Program opens 16 September 2026. Submissions must be received by 11:59 PM local time for applicant on Wednesday, 30 September 2026. Applications that are incomplete or late will not be considered, and neither Alamar nor Geneworks is responsible for applications lost, delayed, misdirected, or not received, except to the extent caused by its own act or omission.
Judges selected by Alamar and Geneworks, who may include their employees and external scientific advisors under confidentiality obligations, will evaluate applications on: access to banked samples with clinical annotations; ability to complete the project within six (6) months of data delivery; and scientific merit and potential for publication in a high-impact peer-reviewed journal.
Recipients will be notified by email on or about three (3) weeks after the closing date (expected during the week of 19 October 2026), and all Applicants will receive confirmation of receipt. A Recipient must respond within ten (10) business days and complete the documentation Alamar and Geneworks reasonably require before services begin, which may include a work plan or service agreement, a material transfer agreement with the entity receiving the samples, and written institutional approval. Failure to respond, ineligibility, or failure to complete that documentation may result in disqualification and selection of an alternate.
**Additional Terms for Australia and New Zealand**
(a) Personal information. Alamar and Geneworks collect Applicants’ names, contact details, and institutional affiliation to administer the Program, and handle that information under the Australian Privacy Principles (Privacy Act 1988 (Cth)), the New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 for NZ Applicants, and Alamar’s Privacy Policy at alamarbio.com. Information is shared between Alamar, Geneworks, and external judges and is transferred to and stored in the United States; by applying, each Applicant consents to that disclosure and transfer. Access and correction requests: alamar@alamarbio,com.
(b) Consumer law. Nothing in these Terms or the General Grant Terms excludes, restricts, or modifies any guarantee, right, or remedy under the Australian Consumer Law, or the New Zealand Consumer Guarantees Act 1993 or Fair Trading Act 1986, that cannot lawfully be excluded. Where liability may be limited, the liability of Alamar and Geneworks is limited, at their option, to re-supplying the analysis services or paying the cost of re-supply.
(c) Research use only. The Panel and all data generated under the Program are for research use only. They are not entered on the Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods or approved as a medical device in New Zealand, and must not be used for diagnosis, treatment, or clinical decision-making, or reported to any research subject or treating clinician.
(d) Governing law. These Terms are governed by the law stated in the General Grant Terms, subject to paragraph (b).

Advertisement

### Dried Blood Spot Extraction Kit
The NULISA™ DBS Extraction Kit provides a standardized, high-throughput workflow for recovering protein analytes from dried blood and dried plasma spots. Combined with NULISA’s attomolar sensitivity, the kit unlocks high-quality multiplexed proteomic data from minimally invasive, remotely collected samples.
[ View Details ](https://alamarbio.com/nulisa-dried-blood-spot-extraction-kit/)
##### Custom Assay Development
### Create Targeted Biomarker Assays
The NULISAqpcr™ Custom Assay Development Kit provides researchers with a flexible solution for creating targeted biomarker assays with high sensitivity and precision. Ideal for applications requiring highly specific and reproducible data, this customizable kit allows scientists to use their own antibodies to create assays tailored to their individual research.
[ Customize your assays ](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/nulisaqpcr-custom-assay-development/)

####  **ARGO Data Analysis Clinics**  
 _A practical enablement series for existing ARGO users_
As **[ARGO™ HT System](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/argo-system/)** adoption and throughput increase, many users are asking similar questions around data outputs, QC, and interpretation. To support our user community, the **Alamar Field Application Scientist (FAS) team** is launching a four‑part virtual enablement series focused on practical aspects of ARGO data analysis.
These sessions are designed to help you better understand your data, troubleshoot common issues, and make more confident decisions.
**What to expect**
  * Monthly **60‑minute virtual sessions**
  * Led by the **Alamar EMEA FAS team**
  * Practical walkthroughs with live Q&A
  * Sessions recorded and available **on demand**
  * Designed for **existing ARGO users**


**Who should attend**
  * ARGO users involved in data review and interpretation
  * Core labs and academic groups running ARGO routinely
  * Anyone seeking a stronger foundation in ARGO data analysis and QC


![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/1080x1080-data-300x300.png)
**Session 1 –[NULISA Analysis Software (NAS)](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/alamar-analysis-solutions/) Fundamentals**  
 _What NAS is and how to use it effectively_  
**On-demand** Passcode: 9F*Ue03K
[ On-Demand - Session 1 ](https://zoom.us/rec/share/NfQuuikDwEYX5AOwJ0_5nBLo9W4K6DtCi5TSP7Do1YvTbIk7xyy3MLBOmPMn5q1p.1Na0fB6wgSyi8dB1)
**Session 2 – Data QC Deep Dive**  
 _Interpreting warnings and understanding QC reports_
**On-demand** Passcode: E7cCh+11
[ ON-DEMAND - Session 2 ](https://zoom.us/rec/share/Nm3pGHIzusbeb8DvmJJBq4rgz1-qp0stJdXzjQWdEdUy22_V9iUHD7or5bVygSA_.8lRfBH7RQCj-OLDp)
**Session 3 –[NULISAseqR](https://nulisaseqr.alamarbio.com/)**  
 _Analysis pipeline walkthrough_
**On-demand**
[ ON-DEMAND - Session 3 ](https://zoom.us/rec/share/j3uzVP-vQ7aTLQ4eu7j2xaxl6R2Vxx514qL58AuusYaI37jENclm8spexF-sg_U2.QDOEVNmkUAQsnmpv)
**Session 4 – NAS with AQ Data**

## About Us
### Our Mission
### Powering precision proteomics to enable the earliest detection of disease.
### Precision proteomics built from experience
Our team of innovators previously created **RNAscope™** , an ultra-sensitive _in situ_ RNA detection technology for spatial genomics.
We have now applied our deep insights into how to maximize signal-to-noise ratio and the latest advances in genomics to create the NULISA technology for ultra-high sensitivity and high specificity analysis of hundreds of protein biomarkers in a single sample from as little as 10 microliters of biofluid.

## Quality & Compliance
### Alamar Biosciences is dedicated to developing and manufacturing under quality systems and standards.
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/13485-2016-SARA-logo-round.jpg)
### ISO 13485:2016
We achieved ISO 13485:2016 certification in 2024, which covers the design and manufacture of medical and laboratory instruments and associated reagents. This achievement underscores our commitment to excellence, safety, and continuous improvement.
[ View certificate ](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/Certificate-ISO-13485.pdf)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/A-LIGN_badge_SOC-2.png)
### SOC 2
Alamar has successfully completed our SOC 2 report with the guidance of third-party audit firm A-LIGN. This comprehensive, globally recognized attestation validates our commitment to critical security standards to protect and secure client data.
### SECURITY TRUST CENTER

metadata.title: ARGO™ HT System | Best High-Throughput Proteomics Platform for Biomarker Discovery
metadata.description: The ARGO™ HT System by Alamar Biosciences delivers fully automated, high-throughput proteomics with ultra-high sensitivity for biomarker discovery. Up to 288 samples per run, results in under 8 hours, and less than 30 minutes hands-on time.
metadata.og:title: ARGO™ HT System | High-Throughput Proteomics Platform for Biomarker Discovery

## ARGO® HT System
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/ARGOTM_HT_System_hotspot.svg) [1](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/argo-system/) [2](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/argo-system/) [3](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/argo-system/)
## Proteomics at the Push of a Button
Engineered for precision and designed for next-generation proteomics, the ARGO® HT system integrates seamless workflows and unparalleled efficiency into one compact solution. Whether you are part of a bustling research lab or an academic institution striving for breakthroughs, the ARGO® HT system is tailored to achieve state-of-the-art liquid biopsy proteomics capabilities with minimal hands-on time.
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/DropGrid_Texture_WhiteFlatUneven-copy-3.svg)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/DropGrid_Texture_WhiteFlatUneven-copy-4.svg)
### ARGO® HT System Features
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/icon-turnkey-instrument-1.svg)
Turnkey instrument
an integrated qPCR system takes you from sample to data or pooled NGS library

#### Bioinformatics Engineer (full time)
Bioinformatics Engineer (full time) – Alamar Biosciences, Inc., 47071 Bayside Pkwy, Fremont, CA 94538. Work location in Fremont, CA. Translate complex biological questions into efficient and effective code, ensuring seamless integration of computational solutions into biological research processes. Collaborate closely with internal R&D teams to identify their specific needs and design data analysis pipelines that streamline and enhance their daily workflows. Serve as a Benchling expert, leveraging the Benchling API to create data analysis and automation algorithms. Contribute to optimizing data management and analysis capabilities using Benchling’s platform. Innovate and construct algorithms tailored to internal process development needs, such as inventory management and Laboratory Information. Actively contribute to the ongoing development and optimization of software tools and workflows, focusing on enhancing efficiency in data analysis and visualization. Engage in continuous improvement efforts to advance existing tools while collaborating with fellow developers to enhance internal software development efforts. Requires a master’s degree in bioinformatics; computational biology, or molecular biology. Experience in developing robust software and pipelines using Python; familiarity with R and Shiny; demonstrate proficiency in software engineering principles, encompassing version control systems such as Git and GitHub, debugging techniques, and comprehensive testing methodologies; exhibit demonstrated expertise in Linux and shell scripting; experience with deployment and containerization environments, with a focus on technologies like Docker.
Salary: $165,131/year. Submit resume and cover letter to Alamar Biosciences, Inc., ATTN: HR, 47071 Bayside Pkwy, Fremont, CA 94538.

### NULISATM assays for Immunology​
Immunology is undergoing a transformative period, driven by advancements in technology and a deeper understanding of the role that the immune system plays in human health and disease. High-sensitivity proteomic technologies are emerging as indispensable tools in the discovery and screening of clinically relevant biomarkers — in the field of immune related disorders.
### Detect More, Quantitate More and Discover More
NULISA assays have demonstrated the ability to measure previously undetectable levels of critical cytokines and researchers are utilizing these assays to make novel discoveries and associations with clinical outcomes.
### NULISA Immunology Grant Program
##### What could you uncover with a more complete view of the immune landscape?
Apply for the **NULISA Immunology Grant Program** for a chance to experience the NULISAseq Immune 340 Panel for your immune-related research.
[ learn more and apply today! ](https://alamarbio.com/nulisa-immunology-grant-immune-340-panel/)
### Key Applications in Precision Immunology
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/icon-immuno-oncology-and-cancer-immunology.svg)
#### Cancer Immunology & Immuno-Oncology
Immuno-oncology has expanded far beyond checkpoint inhibitors. CAR-T, T-cell engagers, cancer vaccines, antibody-drug conjugates, and combination regimens each activate distinct immune mechanisms: cytotoxic cascades, cytokine release, innate-adaptive crosstalk, and bystander responses. Comprehensive biomarker profiling across checkpoint receptors, the TNF superfamily, and the myeloid suppressor landscape is essential for researching mechanisms associated with treatment response, resistance, and immune-related toxicities such as cytokine release syndrome, neurotoxicity, vascular toxicity, and multi-organ immune toxicity.
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/icon-acute-chronic-inflammation.svg)
#### Acute and Chronic Inflammation
Acute inflammatory flares in COPD, asthma, IBD/Crohn’s, and atopic dermatitis are not simply excess inflammation; they reflect dysregulation of distinct immune axes. COPD exacerbations are driven by neutrophilic and macrophage-dominated innate responses amplified by proteolytic tissue destruction. Severe asthma flares involve type 2 alarmin cascades or type 17/neutrophilic mechanisms depending on endotype. IBD flares are mediated by the Th17/IL-23 axis and TNF-driven mucosal damage. Atopic dermatitis is characterized by a type 2 alarmin cascade with chronic barrier dysfunction. Simultaneous measurement of these axes can help researchers characterize pathway activity across disease cohorts and investigate mechanisms associated with therapeutic response.
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/icon-autoimmunity-and-tolerance.svg)
#### Autoimmunity & Tolerance
Autoimmune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, multiple sclerosis, and type 1 diabetes are driven by proteins that often circulate at extremely low abundance. Type I interferons in SLE operate at fg/mL levels, below the detection floor of standard multiplex platforms. Shed co-inhibitory receptors, active cleaved caspases, and complement cleavage products all require ultrasensitive measurement to accurately reflect disease activity, predict therapeutic response, and distinguish one autoimmune endotype from another. Capturing the full complement cascade, BAFF/APRIL axis, and low-abundance interferon signatures enables the precision profiling that translational research studies increasingly require.
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/icon-infectious-disease.svg)
#### Infectious Disease
Infectious disease immunology research demands both breadth and sensitivity. Antiviral responses require discrimination between type I interferons (IFNα/β, systemic antiviral) and type III interferons (IFNλ, mucosal barrier defense), signals that differ in biological relevance fro COVID-19, influenza, and RSV severity stratification but fall below the detection floor of standard platforms. Sepsis research benefits from simultaneous profiling of innate activation and immune suppression to study disease-state transitions and host-response dynamics. For emerging infections, where the pathogen is unknown and the immune response unpredictable, broad, unbiased profiling is an important approach, providing the immune context no targeted assay can match.
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/icon-systemic-immunology-and-aging.svg)
#### Systemic Immunology & Aging
Aging and age-related diseases, including cardiovascular, metabolic, neurodegenerative, and cancer, share a common immune thread: inflammaging. Systemic immune dysregulation in aging is diffuse and interconnected, driven by senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) cytokines, myeloid reprogramming, and progressive immune contraction. Neuroinflammation in conditions such as Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, ALS, and MS requires integrated immune and neurological profiling from the same sample, tracking microglial activation markers alongside neuroprotective factors. Population health and biobank studies require comprehensive immune readouts at sensitivity levels standard platforms cannot reach, enabling discovery research that targeted panels cannot support.

# Alamar Lunch & Learn at University of Alabama at Birmingham
January 22, 2026
Birmingham, AL, USA
###### Topic:
###### Booth:
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/375px-UAB_monogram.png)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/UAB-logo.png)
## Summary
**Tinsley Harrison Tower  
Rm 740  
**1900 University Blvd  
Birmingham, AL 35294**  
**
_*Lunch will be provided_
#### Unlocking the Power of Fluid Biomarkers
Join Alamar Biosciences for a Lunch & Learn seminar at University of Alabama at Birmingham to discover how the [NULISA™ Platform](https://alamarbio.com/technology/nulisa-platform/) and [ARGO™ HT System](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/argo-system/) are transforming research in CNS diseases and beyond. This seminar will offer an open discussion on how Alamar’s tools can support and accelerate your work.
The NULISA™ Platform delivers ultra-high sensitivity, broad dynamic range, and high multiplexing capabilities for precise biomarker detection and quantitation. Paired with the ARGO™ HT System—a fully automated, high-throughput platform capable of generating single-plex results in under 8 hours and multiplex results in under 15 hours—researchers can achieve faster, more reliable data with minimal hands-on time.
Don’t miss this opportunity to engage with experts from Alamar Biosciences for a lively discussion on the cutting-edge capabilities of NULISA and the ARGO HT System.
### Agenda

CHECK IN & LUNCH
#####  **12:00-12:45 pm  
**INTRODUCTION + CASE STUDY
  * **Alamar Bio & NULISA Technology**
  * **Ultrasensitive Biomarker Detection for Neurogenerative Disease, Oncology and Beyond with NULISA**

# Alamar Lunch & Learn Seminar at Mayo Clinic – Jacksonville
February 4, 2026
Jacksonville, FL, USA
11:45 am – 1:00 pm
###### Topic:
###### Booth:
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Mayo-Clinic-Logo-2001-1024x623-1-1-e1768259299392.webp)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/MayoClinic-logo.jpg)
## Event Details
**Birdsall 142  
**4500 San Pablo Rd S  
Jacksonville, FL 32224
_*Lunch will be provided_
#### Unlocking the Power of Fluid Biomarkers
Join Alamar Biosciences for a Lunch & Learn seminar at the Mayo Clinic, Jacksonville to discover how the [NULISA™ Platform](https://alamarbio.com/technology/nulisa-platform/) and [ARGO™ HT System](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/argo-system/) are transforming research in CNS diseases and beyond. This seminar will offer an open discussion on how Alamar’s tools can support and accelerate your work.
The NULISA™ Platform delivers ultra-high sensitivity, broad dynamic range, and high multiplexing capabilities for precise biomarker detection and quantitation. Paired with the ARGO™ HT System—a fully automated, high-throughput platform capable of generating single-plex results in under 8 hours and multiplex results in under 15 hours—researchers can achieve faster, more reliable data with minimal hands-on time.
Don’t miss this opportunity to engage with experts from Alamar Biosciences for a lively discussion on the cutting-edge capabilities of NULISA and the ARGO HT System.
### Agenda

CHECK IN & LUNCH
#####  **12:00-12:45 pm

  * **Alamar Bio & NULISA Technology**
  * **Ultrasensitive Biomarker Detection for Neurogenerative Disease, Oncology and Beyond with NULISA**

# Alamar Precision Biomarker Summit – Houston
February 25, 2026
Houston, TX
11:30 am – 3:00 pm CT
###### Topic:
###### Booth:
## Event Details
##### Blossom Hotel Houston, Curio Collection by Hilton  
7118 Bertner Ave  
Houston, TX 77030
#### Unlock the Power of Fluid Biomarkers
Join Alamar Biosciences and Key Opinion Leaders from local biotechs for a discussion on the latest advances in protein biomarker research with an introduction to NULISA: A precision proteomics platform with ultra-high sensitivity and high multiplex from blood. Learn how scientists are utilizing this novel technology to help advance their protein research.
Don’t miss this opportunity to engage with experts in the field for a lively discussion on how the **NULISA™ Platform** and **ARGO™ HT System** can support and accelerate your research.

# Identifying co-pathologies in Alzheimer’s disease and related Dementias using NULISA
March 4, 2026
6:00 am PT / 9:00 am ET / 2:00 pm GMT
###### Topic:
###### Neurology
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://www.labroots.com/webinar/identifying-co-pathologies-alzheimer-s-disease-related-dementias-using-nulisa)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/LabrootsNeuro26-1.png)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/LabrootsNeuro26-1.png)
### Speaker
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/CarlosCruchaga-300x300.jpg)
Carlos Cruchaga, PhD
Director, NeuroGenomics and Informatics Center
Washington University School of Medicine
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/AlexForrestHay_crop2.png-300x300.jpg)
Alex Forrest-Hay
Senior Vice President, Sales
Alamar Biosciences


## Summary
##### Exploring Co-Pathologies in Alzheimer’s Disease Through High-Multiplex Proteomics
Join us for a webinar on recent advances in blood-based biomarkers for neurodegenerative diseases. **Dr. Carlos Cruchaga** will present novel findings utilizing Alamar Biosciences’ highly sensitive [**NULISA™**](https://alamarbio.com/technology/nulisa-platform/) immunoassay technology in the identification of co-pathologies across neurodegenerative diseases using large-scale AI classification to aid in the development of protein-based diagnostic and prognostic assays.
This presentation will examine how multiplex proteomic analysis is generating valuable insights into Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and other neurodegenerative disorders, contributing critical data for early detection, differential diagnosis, and disease monitoring. Furthermore, Alex Forrest-Hay, Senior Vice President at Alamar Biosciences, will provide an overview of Alamar’s innovative NULISA technology and its significance in advancing discoveries within neurodegenerative research.
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://www.labroots.com/webinar/identifying-co-pathologies-alzheimer-s-disease-related-dementias-using-nulisa)

# Alamar Lunch & Learn Seminar with Merck South San Francisco
January 29, 2026
South San Francisco, CA
12:30 pm – 2:00 pm
###### Topic:
###### Booth:
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Merck-SSF.png)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Merck-thumbnail.png)
## Seminar Details
#####  **Merck Research Laboratories**  
213 E Grand Ave.  
South San Francisco, CA 94080
Join Alamar Biosciences at **Merck South San Francisco** for an afternoon seminar to discover how the [**NULISA™ Platform**](https://alamarbio.com/technology/nulisa-platform/) and [**ARGO™ HT System**](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/argo-system/) are transforming research in CNS diseases and beyond. This seminar will offer an open discussion on how Alamar’s tools can support and accelerate your work.
The NULISA™ Platform delivers ultra-high sensitivity, broad dynamic range, and high multiplexing capabilities for precise biomarker detection and quantitation. Paired with the ARGO™ HT System—a fully automated, high-throughput platform capable of generating single-plex results in under 8 hours and multiplex results in under 15 hours—researchers can achieve faster, more reliable data with minimal hands-on time.
Don’t miss this opportunity to engage with experts from Alamar Biosciences for a lively discussion on the cutting-edge capabilities of NULISA™ and the ARGO™ HT System.
##### _**NULISA Assay Platform – Highest sensitivity single- to high-plex biomarker analysis of soluble proteins and fluid biomarkers in preclinical and clinical development.**_

# Blood and Beyond: Unlocking Biological Insights from Novel Sample Types
February 4, 2026
8:00 am PT / 11:00 am ET / 4:00 pm GMT
###### Topic:
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://xtalks.com/webinars/blood-and-beyond-unlocking-biological-insights-from-novel-sample-types/)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/xtalks_logo.webp)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/NiyatiJhaveri.jpg)
### Speaker
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/NiyatiJhaveri.jpg)
Niyati Jhaveri, PhD
Manager, Technology Access Program
Alamar Biosciences


## Summary
##### Explore how ultra-sensitive proteomics is transforming biomarker discovery beyond traditional blood-based analyses.
The presentation will showcase how NULISA® technology and the ARGO™ HT System enable high-plex, ultra-sensitive protein detection across a wide range of novel and minimally invasive sample types, including dried blood and plasma spots.
The featured speaker, Dr. Niyati Jhaveri, Manager of the Technology Access Program at Alamar Biosciences, will discuss real-world translational and preclinical examples demonstrating how multiplexed proteomics can uncover disease-specific biology, assess therapeutic response and support scalable population-level research.
Join this webinar to learn how ultra-sensitive proteomic profiling from minimally invasive samples is reshaping disease biology and treatment insights across immunology, neuroscience and translational research.
**Attendees will:**
  * Discover how ultra-sensitive proteomics are expanding beyond blood to generate insights from low-volume and non-traditional sample types, including dried blood spots
  * Learn how NULISA technology delivers high-quality, multiplexed protein data from minimally invasive samples, enabling scalable studies without sacrificing sensitivity
  * Explore real-world examples showing how advanced proteomic profiling reveals disease biology and treatment effects across immunology, neurosciences and translational research


[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://xtalks.com/webinars/blood-and-beyond-unlocking-biological-insights-from-novel-sample-types/)

# Unlocking Ultra-Sensitive Proteomics with NULISA Technology
April 28, 2026
Bronx, New York
11:45 am – 1:00 pm
###### Topic:
###### Booth:
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ICTR_Logo.png)
## Introduction to the NULISA Assay Platform
**Albert Einstein College of Medicine**  
1300 Morris Park Ave.  
Forchheimer Building, 1st Floor Lecture Hall  
Bronx, NY 10461
_*lunch catered by Battaglia’s Market_
**_Now available at the Biomarker and Biorepository Core of the Institute for Clinical and Translational Research at Einstein & Montefiore_**
Join Alamar Biosciences for an upcoming seminar at the _**Albert Einstein College of Medicine**_ introducing the [**NULISA™ Platform**](https://alamarbio.com/technology/nulisa-platform/) and [**ARGO™ HT System**](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/argo-system/), now available to support your proteomics research.
The session will introduce the technology’s ultra-sensitive, high-multiplex capabilities and how it enables deeper protein insights from small volumes of biofluid. Don’t miss the opportunity to engage with Alamar experts for a lively discussion on the cutting-edge capabilities of the platform and ARGO™ HT System.
