# Lunch & Learn Seminar with Alamar at The Montreal Neurological Institute
March 24, 2026
Montreal, Quebec, Canada
11:00 am – 1:00 pm
###### Topic:
###### Booth:
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/images.png)
## Seminar Details
**Jeanne Timmins Amphitheatre**  
The Neuro – 3801 University Street  
Montreal, Quebec H3A 2B4
#### Discover High Sensitivity Proteomics with Alamar at The Montreal Neurological Institute
Join Alamar Biosciences for a lunch & learn seminar at **The Montreal Neurological Institute** to discover how the [NULISA™ Platform](https://alamarbio.com/technology/nulisa-platform/) and [ARGO™ HT System](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/argo-system/) are transforming research in CNS diseases and beyond. This seminar will offer an open discussion on how Alamar’s tools can support and accelerate your work.
The NULISA™ Platform delivers ultra-high sensitivity, broad dynamic range, and high multiplexing capabilities for precise biomarker detection and quantitation. Paired with the ARGO™ HT System—a fully automated, high-throughput platform capable of generating single-plex results in under 8 hours and multiplex results in under 15 hours—researchers can achieve faster, more reliable data with minimal hands-on time.
Don’t miss this opportunity to engage with experts from Alamar Biosciences for a lively discussion on the cutting-edge capabilities of NULISA™ and the ARGO™ HT System.
Visit Event Site

April 16, 2026

3:00 pm – 4:00 pm

###### Booth:

## Event Details
**Pagano Conference Room**  
UNC Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center  
450 West Drive  
Chapel Hill, NC, United States
Join Alamar Biosciences for an upcoming seminar at **UNC at Chapel Hill** to explore how the [NULISA™ Platform](https://alamarbio.com/technology/nulisa-platform/) and [ARGO™ HT System ](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/argo-system/)are enabling ultrasensitive fluid biomarker detection across immunology, oncology, neurology, and beyond. # Precision Biomarker Signatures Enhanced with Ultra Sensitive NULISA
April 27, 2026
Lexington, KY
12:00 pm – 1:30 pm ET
###### Topic:
###### Booth:
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/UK-college-of-med.png)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/UK-college-of-med.png)
## Event Details
**University of Kentucky College of Medicine**  
**HKRB 150 (Healthy Kentucky Research Building)**  
760 Press Avenue  
Lexington KY 40536  
_*lunch provided_
Join Alamar Biosciences for an upcoming seminar at the **University of Kentucky College of Medicine** to discover how the [NULISA™ Platform](https://alamarbio.com/technology/nulisa-platform/) and [ARGO™ HT System](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/argo-system/) are transforming research in CNS diseases and beyond. The session will highlight recent research using the [NULISAqpcr™ BD-pTau217 Assay](https://alamarbio.com/nulisaqpcr-bd-ptau217-assay/), showcasing advances in detecting critical biomarkers to better understand disease biology and mechanisms of action.
Built on attomolar sensitivity and high-multiplex detection, NULISA™ enables ultra-sensitive profiling of biofluid biomarkers, supporting translational studies and emerging clinical applications.
Don’t miss this opportunity to engage with experts from Alamar Biosciences for a lively discussion on the cutting-edge capabilities of **NULISA™** and the**ARGO™ HT System**.

San Diego, CA, US 92121
Join Alamar Biosciences for an upcoming seminar at **Johnson & Johnson** in San Diego to explore how the [NULISA™ Platform](https://alamarbio.com/technology/nulisa-platform/) and [ARGO™ HT System](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/argo-system/) are advancing immunology and inflammation research. This session will include a presentation on NULISA™ and its applications in immunology, alongside an open discussion on how Alamar’s tools can support and accelerate your work.
We’ll also highlight how NULISA enables sensitive, high-multiplex profiling of cytokines and inflammatory biomarkers from small sample volumes, supporting deeper insights in translational and clinical research.
Don’t miss this opportunity to engage with experts from Alamar over coffee & donuts for a lively discussion on the cutting-edge capabilities of NULISA™ and the ARGO™ HT System.
Visit Event Site

#### "Goldilocks” Proteomics: How NULISA delivers “just right” discovery power
Steve Williams, MD, PhD
CSO
Alamar Biosciences

## Event Details
**AbbVie – Irvine**  
2525 Dupont Drive  
Irvine, CA
Join Alamar Biosciences for an upcoming seminar at **AbbVie** in Irvine to discover how the [NULISA™ Platform](https://alamarbio.com/technology/nulisa-platform/) and [ARGO™ HT System](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/argo-system/) are transforming research in CNS diseases and beyond. This seminar will offer an open discussion on how Alamar’s tools can support and accelerate your work.
The NULISA™ Platform delivers ultra-high sensitivity, broad dynamic range, and high multiplexing capabilities for precise biomarker detection and quantitation. Paired with the ARGO™ HT System—a fully automated, high-throughput platform capable of generating single-plex results in under 8 hours and multiplex results in under 15 hours—researchers can achieve faster, more reliable data with minimal hands-on time.
Don’t miss this opportunity to engage with experts from Alamar over lunch for a lively discussion on the cutting-edge capabilities of NULISA™ and the ARGO™ HT System.

## Event Details
**Gilead Sciences  
**Darwin CR B324  
1st Floor
Join Alamar Biosciences for an upcoming seminar at **Gilead** to discover how the [NULISA™ Platform](https://alamarbio.com/technology/nulisa-platform/) and [ARGO™ HT System](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/argo-system/) are transforming research in CNS diseases and beyond. This seminar will offer an open discussion on how Alamar’s tools can support and accelerate your work.
The NULISA™ Platform delivers ultra-high sensitivity, broad dynamic range, and high multiplexing capabilities for precise biomarker detection and quantitation. Paired with the ARGO™ HT System—a fully automated, high-throughput platform capable of generating single-plex results in under 8 hours and multiplex results in under 15 hours—researchers can achieve faster, more reliable data with minimal hands-on time.
Don’t miss this opportunity to engage with experts from Alamar over lunch for a lively discussion on the cutting-edge capabilities of NULISA™ and the ARGO™ HT System.

# Precision Proteomics Applications to Enhance Immune Oncology Therapeutics
April 29, 2026
9:00 am PT / 12 pm ET / 4pm GMT
###### Topic:
######  Immunology, Oncology
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://www.labroots.com/virtual-event/immuno-oncology-2026)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Labroots-IO-image.jpg)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Labroots-IO-image.jpg)
### Presenter
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Steve-williams.png)
Steve Williams, MD, PhD
CSO
Alamar Biosciences


## Summary
Fluid-based biomarkers are increasingly critical for predicting therapeutic response and adverse events in immuno-oncology, where patient heterogeneity drives variable outcomes. Traditional tissue biopsies are limited by invasiveness and sampling bias, highlighting the need for scalable, noninvasive approaches. Genetic assays provide information about the tumor burden but not about the immune response. [NULISA Technology ](https://alamarbio.com/technology/nulisa-platform/)overcomes these challenges through ultra-sensitive, multiplexed protein detection from small volumes of blood, enabling robust quantification of low-abundance biomarkers across a wide dynamic range. This capability supports longitudinal monitoring of immune activity, early identification of responders and non-responders, and detection of toxicity signals. By providing precise, reproducible measurements, NULISA empowers more informed clinical decisions, enhances trial design, and advances personalized immunotherapy strategies.

# Unlocking the Power of Fluid Biomarkers in Neurological Disease and Stroke
July 22, 2026
Calgary, AB, Canada
12:15 pm – 1:30 pm MDT
###### Topic:
###### Booth:
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/UCalgary_Vertical_logo_colour_1.jpg)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/UCalgary_Vertical_logo_colour_1.jpg)
## Event Details
**Hotchkiss Brain Institute, University of Calgary**  
**Health Sciences Centre – Room 1405A**
_*lunch provided_
Join Alamar Biosciences at the University of Calgary for a lunch seminar exploring how the [NULISA™ Platform](https://alamarbio.com/technology/nulisa-platform/) and [ARGO™ HT System](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/argo-system/) are advancing fluid biomarker research in neurodegenerative diseases. Learn how ultra-sensitive precision proteomics is enabling earlier detection, deeper biological insights, and translational biomarker discovery across CNS diseases and beyond.
This interactive session will highlight real-world research applications and demonstrate how NULISA™ technology can support your work—from biomarker discovery through clinical translation. Bring your questions and join the discussion with Alamar experts to explore how these tools can accelerate your research.
Visit Event Site

# Unlocking the Power of Ultrasensitive Fluid Biomarkers – Proteomic Profiling Across Systems and Diseases
July 28, 2026
Miami, FL
11:30 am – 1:00 pm EDT
###### Topic:
###### Booth:
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/university-of-miami-logo-vector.png)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/university-of-miami-logo-vector.png)
## Event Details
**The University of Miami – Miller School of Medicine**  
Biomedical Research Building  
3rd Floor Atrium  
501 NW 10th Ave., Miami, FL 33136
_*lunch provided_
Join Alamar Biosciences at the University of Miami for a seminar exploring how the [NULISA™ Platform](https://alamarbio.com/technology/nulisa-platform/) and [ARGO™ HT System](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/argo-system/) are enabling ultrasensitive fluid biomarker detection and proteomic profiling across neurology, immunology, oncology, and beyond. The session will highlight broad research applications and how these technologies can support translational biomarker discovery across systems and diseases.
Don’t miss this opportunity to engage with experts from Alamar Biosciences for a lively discussion on the cutting-edge capabilities of NULISA™ and the ARGO™ HT System.
Visit Event Site

University of Miami
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Sruthi-headshot-300x300.jpg)
Sruthi Sivakumar, PhD
Field Application Scientist
Alamar Biosciences

# New Proteomics Technology Brings Unprecedented Sensitivity and Scale: Yuling Luo, CEO, Alamar Bio
###### Topic:
###### Booth:
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Mendels-pod-logo.png)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Mendels-pod-logo.png)
## Summary
Yuling Luo is a serial entrepreneur who has founded three significant companies in life science tools. Most recently, he is the founder and CEO of Alamar Biosciences, which commercially launched its ARGO HT instrument this year, as well as a powerful new panel to detect inflammatory proteins called NULISA.
Before founding Alamar, Luo was the founder and CEO of Advanced Cell Diagnostics, which was acquired by BioTechne in 2016. He was also a co-founder of Panomics, which was scooped up by Affymetrix.
Yuling recently lost his mother to cancer and feels the compelling case that we can do better with early detection. In founding Alamar, he realized this was really a technical problem.
He says that “liquid biopsy is quite popular, but the performance is limited. Detection for stage I cancer is 25 percent. That is not good enough. We need to get to 80 to 90 percent for it to really be meaningful. Why not use proteins for markers?” he asked. “There are hundreds of thousands to millions of copies of proteins. And proteins are more specific to tissue type.”
How does the new Alamar technology work and fit in the overall proteomics tools landscape? Yuling says it is more sensitive and able to detect 90 percent of the proteins in blood plasma, up from 50 percent with other tools. The new sensitivity comes from suppressing background noise 10,000-fold.
How is Alamar’s technology impacting research in the hot areas of Alzheimer’s and inflammatory disease? What is the overall opportunity with this new sensitivity? And what is the biggest challenge for the company over the next couple of years?

Honolulu, HI, USA
12:00 pm – 1:00 pm HST

###### Booth:

## Event Details
**The University of Hawai’i Cancer Center**  
UHCC-4B-401 Conference Room  
701 Ilalo St, Honolulu, HI 96813
_*lunch provided_
Join Alamar Biosciences for a lunch & learn seminar at the **University of Hawai’i Cancer Center** to discover how the [NULISA™ Platform](https://alamarbio.com/technology/nulisa-platform/) and[ ARGO™ HT System](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/argo-system/) are advancing biomarker research across a broad range of diseases and applications. This seminar will offer an open discussion on how Alamar’s technologies can support and accelerate your research.
Don’t miss this opportunity to connect with experts from Alamar Biosciences and learn more about the cutting-edge capabilities of NULISA™ and the ARGO™ HT System.

# Alamar Lunch & Learn seminar at TMIC, University of Alberta
October 6, 2026
Edmonton, AB, Canada
12:30 pm – 1:45 pm
###### Topic:
###### Booth:
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/TMIC-logo.png)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/TMIC-logo.png)
## Event Details
**Gunning Lemieux Chemistry Centre**  
**Room E3-25**  
11227 Saskatchewan Dr NW  
Edmonton, AB T6G 2G2
_*lunch provided_
Join Alamar Biosciences at **TMIC at the University of Alberta** for a seminar exploring how the [NULISA™ Platform](https://alamarbio.com/technology/nulisa-platform/) and [ARGO™ HT System](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/argo-system/) are enabling ultrasensitive fluid biomarker detection and proteomic profiling across neurology, immunology, oncology, and beyond. The session will highlight broad research applications and how these technologies can support translational biomarker discovery across systems and diseases.
Don’t miss this opportunity to engage with experts from Alamar Biosciences for a lively discussion on the cutting-edge capabilities of NULISA™ and the ARGO™ HT System.
Visit Event Site

# Biomarkers of Aging Conference 2026
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Screenshot-2026-09-18-124840.png)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Screenshot-2026-09-18-124840.png)
October 5 – October 6, 2026
Boston, MA
###### Topic:
######  Immunology, Neurology
### Join Alamar Biosciences at the Biomarkers of Aging Conference
The Biomarkers of Aging Consortium supports the global geroscience community by creating standardized, clinically validated ways to measure aging and assess intervention outcomes. Its work helps give the field the tools needed to turn longevity interventions into safe and effective therapies.
Alamar Biosciences is excited to join researchers and leaders across the geroscience community to explore advances in aging biology, biomarker measurement, and technologies helping move geroscience discoveries toward translation.
While at the meeting, don’t miss a poster presentation from **Xiao-Jun Ma, Ph.D., Chief Technology Officer at Alamar Biosciences** , featuring research enabled by NULISA™ technology.
**Monday, October 5 | 12:20–12:55 PM ET**  
**Auditorium | The Joseph B. Martin Conference Center at Harvard Medical School**
Connect with the Alamar team at the meeting to learn more about how our **NULISA™ and ARGO® HT platforms** enable ultra-sensitive, multiplex protein detection and support deeper investigation of the low-abundance proteome.
### Poster Presentation
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Xiao-JunMa_crop-300x300.png)
#### A 62-Protein Plasma Module Spanning Brain and Immune Arms Predicts Accelerated Aging and Mortality
Xiao-Jun Ma
Chief Technology Officer
Alamar Biosciences

September 23, 2026
3:00 pm – 4:00 pm BST
###### Topic:
###### Data Analysis
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://zoom.us/rec/share/6Hw9xnWkdAcDMvk7maornxLBsShX0j9tTX8P6XrIG7qT3D2L7t09BD_vVIuxlKdb.6pKenZKifLVRsJZk)

  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Dan-Frederick.jpg)
Daniel Frederick
Snr. Field Application Scientist
Alamar Biosciences


## Summary
**NAS with AQ Data |**_Advanced analysis workflows using AQ data_
**Wednesday, 24 September | 3PM BST / 4PM CEST / 10AM EDT**
As [ARGO™ HT System](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/argo-system/) adoption and throughput increase, many users are asking similar questions around data outputs, QC, and interpretation. To support our user community, the Alamar Field Application Scientist (FAS) team is launching a four‑part virtual enablement series focused on practical aspects of ARGO data analysis. The series reaches its conclusion with an analysis of advanced workflows using AQ data from the [NULISAseq™ Inflammation Panel AQ](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/nulisa-inflammation-panel-aq/).
These sessions are designed to help you better understand your data, troubleshoot common issues, and make more confident decisions.
**What to expect**
  * Monthly **60‑minute virtual sessions**
  * Led by the **Alamar EMEA FAS team**
  * Practical walkthroughs with live Q&A
  * Sessions recorded and available **on demand**
  * Designed for **existing ARGO users**


**Who should attend**
  * ARGO users involved in data review and interpretation
  * Core labs and academic groups running ARGO routinely
  * Anyone seeking a stronger foundation in ARGO data analysis and QC


**Past sessions include (view on-demand)**
  * [**NULISA Analysis Software (NAS) Fundamentals**](https://alamarbio.com/event/argo-data-analysis-clinic-nulisa-analysis-software-nas-fundamentals/)
  * [**Data QC Deep Dive**](https://alamarbio.com/event/argo-data-analysis-clinic-data-qc-deep-dive/)
  * **[NULISAseqR](https://alamarbio.com/event/argo-data-analysis-clinic-nulisaseqr/)**

# A Blood Test for Alzheimer’s Disease – Thinking Beyond a Diagnosis
Online
###### Topic:
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://www.labroots.com/webinar/blood-test-alzheimer-s-disease-thinking-beyond-diagnosis)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/virtual_event_profile_image_99a0dd4eb5a626def38ae9f13e0f652fc610ec8f_5771.jpg)
### Speaker
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/NickAshton-300x300.png)
Nicholas Ashton, PhD
Associate Professor of Neurochemistry
University of Gothenburg
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/AlexForrestHay_crop2.png-300x300.jpg)
Alex Forrest-Hay
VP of Sales
Alamar Biosciences


The advancement in ultra-sensitive immunoassays and highly specific immunoprecipitation mass spectrometry (IPMS) methods, complimented by an increasing number of well-characterised research cohorts adhering to a biological definition of disease, have substantially contributed to the rapid development of reliability quantifying key targets in blood plasma or serum samples. In Alzheimer’s disease (AD), measures of phosphorylated tau (p-tau), particularly p-tau217, have now shown great utility in identifying cerebral pathology at all stages of the disease continuum. Thus, it is anticipated that plasma p-tau217 will be an important component of patient management and treatments decisions related to AD. Yet, there remains a multitude of biomarker applications in AD, and related disorders, where plasma p-tau217 may not be fully sufficient. Therefore, a new period of proteomic biomarker discovery has begun, centered around p-tau, NfL, and GFAP, to address these needs.
This session will briefly overview the rapid development of blood biomarkers for AD, with a focus on phosphorylated tau. The talk will then highlight areas of need in biomarkers development, in the era of disease-modifying trials. We will conclude by looking at the capabilities of NULISA at the singleplex and multiplex level, and case-studies in how this novel technology may begin to address new biomarkers challenages that are emerging.

# Advances in High Sensitivity Protein Detection from Biofluids and the Potential in Early Diagnosis and Therapeutic Monitoring
April 30, 2025
Online
###### Topic:
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://www.labroots.com/webinar/panel-presentation-advances-sensitivity-protein-detection-biofluids-potential-diagnosis-therapeutic)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/LabrootsIO2024.jpg)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/YuehanFeng.png)
### Presenters
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/YuehanFeng_100.png)
Yuehan Feng, PhD
Sr. Director, Application Sciences
Biognosys
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/xiao-jun-ma.jpg)
Xiao-Jun Ma, PhD
Chief Technology Officer
Alamar Biosciences
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/AlexForrestHay_crop2.png-300x300.jpg)
Alex Forrest-Hay
VP of Sales
Alamar Biosciences


## Summary
Circulating proteins found in biofluids represent ideal biomarkers for early disease detection and can be collected non-invasively. Detection from biofluids, however, is challenging as highly abundant proteins mask the detection of low abundance proteins involved in the regulation of key biochemical cascades. The NULISA™ Platform improves the sensitivity of traditional immunoassays and provides highly multiplexed quantification of both low- and high-abundance proteins from the same 10uL sample. The NULISAseq™ Inflammation Panel 250 provides deep coverage of cytokines and markers of immune response enabling the discovery of signatures of disease progression, disease heterogeneity, or to predict the development of serious reactions.

  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/AlexForrestHay_crop2.png-300x300.jpg)
Alex Forrest-Hay
Senior Vice President, Sales
Alamar Biosciences


## Summary
In this webinar, Jonathan Schott and Alex Forrest-Hay will showcase how new biomarker assays for brain-derived pTau217 capture disease-relevant changes earlier and with greater resolution.
Amyloid plaques and Tau tangles are a key pathological feature of Alzheimer’s Disease (AD), and increased phosphorylated Tau217 (pTau217) levels have proven to be a robust biomarker for this condition. Measuring brain-derived pTau from plasma samples with high sensitivity and specificity is shown to improve the accuracy of detecting AD and reduce the percentage of samples in the indeterminant range.
In this webinar, brought to you by Alamar Biosciences, Jonathan Schott and Alex Forrest-Hay will discuss the latest ultra-sensitive assays for measuring brain-derived pTau217 and outline how they are transforming the detection and prediction of AD.
****Topics to be covered****
  * The role of brain-derived biomarkers in improving AD detection
  * The development and performance of high-sensitivity nucleic acid-linked immuno-sandwich assays for CNS disease
  * Comparison of assay performance to standard assays in real-world samples

# Alzheimer’s Disease: Early Detection and Multi-Etiology Insights from Blood-Based Immunoassays
###### Topic:
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://www.workcast.com/register?cpak=3084180033225336&referrer=200)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/GENlogo_ColorBackground_062618_200.png)
### Speaker
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/SterlingJohnson2-300x300.jpg)
Sterling Johnson, PhD
Professor of Geriatrics and Dementia
Department of Geriatrics and Gerontology, University of Wisconsin
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/AlexForrestHay_crop2.png-300x300.jpg)
Alex Forrest-Hay
VP of Sales
Alamar Biosciences


Detecting Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) before the symptoms of cognitive decline begin is essential for effective prevention. Highly sensitive, multiplex blood-based immunoassays can help with early-stage disease studies as well as with unraveling the complex mix of AD-associated etiologies. The result is more informed patient stratification for clinical trials, improved diagnosis and prognosis, and faster treatment discovery.
In this GEN webinar, our expert speaker, Dr. Sterling Johnson, will discuss multi-plex blood biomarker assays, new discoveries in AD research from a large-scale study, and opportunities for early intervention during the presymptomatic phase of the disease. In the first part of the webinar, he’ll use data from the Wisconsin Registry for Alzheimer’s Prevention (WRAP) study, which follows healthy middle-aged volunteers at increased risk of AD, to discuss ways of identifying when AD begins at the individual-level based on PET, CSF and blood-based biomarkers assessed using the immunoassay technology, NULISA™.
The second part of the webinar will focus on opportunities for learning more about other factors in the brain that contribute to cognitive decline in AD cases. Dr. Johnson will discuss the mixture of etiologies that co-occur with AD including vascular disease, alpha synuclein proteinopathy, and/or TDP43 proteinopathy, and how NULISA assays can elucidate multi-etiology cognitive impairment and antecedent states that present clinically as AD. You’ll also hear from Alex Forrest-Hay who will share details about Alamar’s technology.

July 8, 2026
Zoom Webinar
3:00 pm – 4:00 am BST
###### Topic:
###### Data Analysis
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://zoom.us/rec/share/Nm3pGHIzusbeb8DvmJJBq4rgz1-qp0stJdXzjQWdEdUy22_V9iUHD7or5bVygSA_.8lRfBH7RQCj-OLDp)

### Speaker
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Doug-Hinerfeld.jpg)
Doug Hinerfeld, PhD.
Senior Director of Application Support
Alamar Biosciences


## Summary
**Data QC Deep Dive |**_Interpreting warnings and understanding QC reports_  
**Wednesday, 8 July | 3PM BST / 4PM CEST / 10AM EDT : Passcode: E7cCh+11**
As [ARGO™ HT System](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/argo-system/) adoption and throughput increase, many users are asking similar questions around data outputs, QC, and interpretation. To support our user community, the Alamar Field Application Scientist (FAS) team is launching a four‑part virtual enablement series focused on practical aspects of ARGO data analysis. Continuing the series with interpreting warnings and understanding QC reports when using the [NULISA Analysis Software (NAS)](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/alamar-analysis-solutions/)
These sessions are designed to help you better understand your data, troubleshoot common issues, and make more confident decisions.
**What to expect**
  * Monthly **60‑minute virtual sessions**
  * Led by the **Alamar EMEA FAS team**
  * Practical walkthroughs with live Q&A
  * Sessions recorded and available **on demand**
  * Designed for **existing ARGO users**


**Who should attend**
  * ARGO users involved in data review and interpretation
  * Core labs and academic groups running ARGO routinely
  * Anyone seeking a stronger foundation in ARGO data analysis and QC


**Future session include**
  * **[NULISAseqR |](https://nulisaseqr.alamarbio.com/) **_Analysis pipeline walkthrough_
  * **NAS with AQ Data |**_Advanced analysis workflows using AQ data_

# ARGO Data Analysis Clinic | NULISA Analysis Software (NAS) Fundamentals
June 3, 2026
Zoom Webinar
3:00 pm – 4:00 am BST
###### Topic:
###### Data Analysis
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://zoom.us/rec/share/NfQuuikDwEYX5AOwJ0_5nBLo9W4K6DtCi5TSP7Do1YvTbIk7xyy3MLBOmPMn5q1p.1Na0fB6wgSyi8dB1)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/NAS_Straight.png)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Data-Analysis-NASFund.png)
### Speaker
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/HS_Mathias-Holpert-300x300.png)
Mathias Holpert, PhD.
Manager, Field Applications Scientist
Alamar Biosciences


## Summary
**NULISA Analysis Software (NAS) Fundamentals |**_What NAS is and how to use it effectively_  
**Wednesday, 3 June | 3PM BST / 4PM CEST / 10AM EDT Passcode: 9F*Ue03K**
As [ARGO™ HT System](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/argo-system/) adoption and throughput increase, many users are asking similar questions around data outputs, QC, and interpretation. To support our user community, the Alamar Field Application Scientist (FAS) team is launching a four‑part virtual enablement series focused on practical aspects of ARGO data analysis. Starting with basics of using the [NULISA Analysis Software (NAS)](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/alamar-analysis-solutions/)
These sessions are designed to help you better understand your data, troubleshoot common issues, and make more confident decisions.
**What to expect**
  * Monthly **60‑minute virtual sessions**
  * Led by the **Alamar EMEA FAS team**
  * Practical walkthroughs with live Q&A
  * Sessions recorded and available **on demand**
  * Designed for **existing ARGO users**


**Who should attend**
  * ARGO users involved in data review and interpretation
  * Core labs and academic groups running ARGO routinely
  * Anyone seeking a stronger foundation in ARGO data analysis and QC


**Future session include**
  * **Data QC Deep Dive |**_Interpreting warnings and understanding QC reports_
  * **[NULISAseqR |](https://nulisaseqr.alamarbio.com/) **_Analysis pipeline walkthrough_
  * **NAS with AQ Data |**_Advanced analysis workflows using AQ data_

## Summary
**NULISAseqR |**_Analysis pipeline walkthrough_  
**Wednesday, 12 August | 3PM BST / 4PM CEST / 10AM EDT**
As [ARGO™ HT System](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/argo-system/) adoption and throughput increase, many users are asking similar questions around data outputs, QC, and interpretation. To support our user community, the Alamar Field Application Scientist (FAS) team is launching a four‑part virtual enablement series focused on practical aspects of ARGO data analysis. Continuing the series with an analysis pipeline walkthrough with [NULISAseqR](https://nulisaseqr.alamarbio.com/).
These sessions are designed to help you better understand your data, troubleshoot common issues, and make more confident decisions.
**What to expect**
  * Monthly **60‑minute virtual sessions**
  * Led by the **Alamar EMEA FAS team**
  * Practical walkthroughs with live Q&A
  * Sessions recorded and available **on demand**
  * Designed for **existing ARGO users**


**Who should attend**
  * ARGO users involved in data review and interpretation
  * Core labs and academic groups running ARGO routinely
  * Anyone seeking a stronger foundation in ARGO data analysis and QC


**Future session include**
  * **NAS with AQ Data |**_Advanced analysis workflows using AQ data_

# Benchmarking of a Multi-biomarker Low-volume Panel for Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementia Research
April 8, 2025
Online
2:00 pm EDT / 11am PDT
###### Topic:
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://xtalks.com/webinars/benchmarking-of-a-multi-biomarker-low-volume-panel-for-alzheimers-disease-and-related-dementia-research/)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/LabrootsIO2024.jpg)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/CarlosCruchaga.jpg)
### Presenters
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Laura-Ibanez-WashU-formatted.jpg)
Laura Ibáñez, PhD
Assistant Professor of Psychiatry
Washington University of Medicine
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/CarlosCruchaga-300x300.jpg)
Carlos Cruchaga, PhD
Professor of Psychiatry
Washington University of Medicine


## Summary
Discover an informative webinar featuring leading researchers as they discuss advancements in biomarker discovery for Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and related dementias.
The expert speakers will present on the validation and application of a highly sensitive and low-volume multiplexed assay designed to detect key neurodegenerative disease biomarkers. They will explore how this platform enhances the measurement of critical Alzheimer’s biomarkers, such as pTau217, offering a minimally invasive and scalable approach for early diagnosis and disease monitoring in both sporadic and autosomal dominant AD.
They will follow with a discussion on large-scale plasma proteomics and its role in identifying disease-specific biomarkers across neurodegenerative diseases, including AD, Parkinson’s disease (PD), dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD). Her research highlights the power of plasma pTau217 as a predictive biomarker for amyloid pathology and the broader impact of proteomic profiling in precision medicine.
This webinar will showcase how the multiplexed assay is setting a new benchmark for biomarker research, enabling high-sensitivity, low-volume detection to transform Alzheimer’s and dementia diagnostics, research and clinical applications.
Register for this webinar to gain insights into highly sensitive multiplexed assay and plasma proteomics for neurodegenerative disease diagnostics.
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://xtalks.com/webinars/benchmarking-of-a-multi-biomarker-low-volume-panel-for-alzheimers-disease-and-related-dementia-research/)

# Comparison of multiplexed platforms for serum cytokine detection in COVID-19 patients
Online
###### Topic:
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://www.labroots.com/ms/webinar/comparison-multiplexed-platforms-serum-cytokine-detection-covid-19-patients)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/Scholarship_Featured_Labroots-768x768-1.png)
### Speaker
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/HoldenMaecker-300x300.png)
Holden Maecker, PhD
Professor (Research), Microbiology & Immunology
Stanford University
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/AlexForrestHay_crop2.png-300x300.jpg)
Alex Forrest-Hay
VP of Sales
Alamar Biosciences


Alamar NULISAseq is a novel commercial platform for highly multiplexed analysis of soluble proteins using a modified proximity ligation assay. We compared Luminex, Olink, and NULISAseq platforms for detection of cytokines and related inflammatory markers in sera from 25 patients with COVID-19 and 8 healthy controls. We analyzed detectability of common targets, correlations between platforms, and identification of differentially expressed targets in COVID-19 patients (versus healthy controls, over time, and with disease severity). We found the highest proportion of detectable targets with NULISAseq, and best correlations between NULISAseq and Olink. Correlations were often better for targets with high detectability. NULISAseq also identified the largest number of significant changes over time in longitudinal COVID-19 samples. Olink identified slightly more differentially expressed targets between healthy and COVID-19 samples, but some of these were, paradoxically, low in detectability in Olink. All three assays were similar in their ability to differentiate COVID-19 severity levels at hospital admission. Overall, our results suggest that NULISAseq is a highly sensitive assay, with good correlation
Learning Objectives
  * To understand the methodology used by major multiplexed immunoassay platforms, and the inherent pros and cons of each.
  * To describe the differences in detectability between assay platforms and how this relates to correlations between platforms.
  * To relate these assay differences to their ability to detect differential protein expression in COVID-19 patients.


[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://www.labroots.com/ms/webinar/comparison-multiplexed-platforms-serum-cytokine-detection-covid-19-patients)

# Comprehensive profiling of 200+ proteins using the NULISAseq Inflammation Panel reveals unique signatures of immune response in AML
Online
###### Topic:
###### Oncology
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://www.labroots.com/webinar/comprehensive-profiling-200-proteins-using-nulisaseq-inflammation-panel-reveals-unique-signatures-im)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Labroot-CRIO-2023.png)
### Speaker
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/HusseinAbbas-300x300.jpg)
Hussein Abbas, PhD
Assistant Professor, Department of Leukemia
Department of Genomic Medicine, UT, MD Anderson Cancer Center
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/AlexForrestHay_crop2.png-300x300.jpg)
Alex Forrest-Hay
VP of Sales
Alamar Biosciences


## Summary
Preliminary data indicate the presence of inflammatory derangements in AML, necessitating a comprehensive examination of inflammatory effector cytokines involved in AML pathogenesis and therapeutic responses. Addressing this issue requires overcoming two major challenges: the existence of over 300 cytokines associated with human disease, and the presence of functional yet low-level cytokines. A high-throughput method capable of characterizing numerous cytokines and identifying potential therapeutic targets is essential, along with a cytokine profiler that captures a wide dynamic level range. We propose utilizing NULISA, a novel method that enables the comprehensive characterization of more than 200 important cytokines and chemokines with ultra-high sensitivity and scalable multiplexing, effectively tackling both challenges. 88 Serum samples from AML and healthy subjects were profiled using Alamar’s NULISAseq 200-plex Inflammation panel. Unsupervised clustering showed different sample groups clustering together and differential expression analysis revealed unique inflammation profiles for AML patients compared to healthy donors. These results revealed that 200-plex Inflammation panel can detect various circulatory inflammatory biomarkers with high sensitivity and specificity and these features can reveal novel biological insights into inflammatory derangements in AML disease.

# Emerging Biomarker Insights Across Immune-Mediated Inflammatory Diseases with NULISA™
September 24, 2026
3:00 pm – 5:30 pm BST
###### Topic:
###### Immunology
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://zoom.us/rec/share/8GDp9MWzqSl3NSyuN0he0hR6gGlXzvKQDetAcuNGL-_tAQxnXi17xT4Rwr3LUZE4.LVDZqrTJz-MY6R6Z)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Immune_Alpha_8K.png)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/IMID-26.png)
### Speaker
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/HS-Chris-Wincup-300x300.png)
Dr. Chris Wincup
Consultant Rheumatologist
King's College London
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/HS-Felix-Wohlrab-300x300.png)
Dr. Felix Wohlrab
Neurologist
Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/HS-Jasmine-Sim-300x300.png)
Dr Jasmine Sim
Research Associate
Translational and Clinical Research Institute, Newcastle University


## Summary
Advances in ultra-sensitive proteomics are transforming our understanding of**immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs)** , enabling researchers to uncover biological signals that were previously difficult to detect and investigate.
Join leading researchers from across Europe for a scientific webinar exploring emerging biomarker insights generated using [**NULISA™ technology**](https://alamarbio.com/technology/nulisa-platform/) across multiple IMID indications. Through a series of research presentations and an expert panel discussion, speakers will share new findings, discuss common disease mechanisms, and explore how highly multiplexed protein profiling is advancing biomarker discovery and translational research.
Whether your work focuses on autoimmune disease, neuroinflammation, immunology, or biomarker development, this session offers an opportunity to learn from investigators actively generating new IMID datasets and applying them to important biological questions.
## Why Attend?
Attendees will have the opportunity to:
  * Hear emerging research findings generated using NULISA™ technology
  * Explore biomarker discovery approaches across multiple IMID indications
  * Gain insight into shared biological and inflammatory pathways across diseases
  * Learn how ultra-sensitive proteomics is supporting translational and clinical research
  * Participate in a live discussion with leading researchers and submit questions during the webinar


## Agenda
**15:00-15:10****Welcome & Introduction | **Overview of the webinar and the growing role of ultra-sensitive proteomics in IMID research.  
**15:10-15:30****Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) |** Emerging biomarker insights from lupus research using NULISA technology. _Chris Wincup_  
**15:30-15:50****Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disease (NMOSD) |** Dried blood spot diagnostics in Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disease (NMOSD). _Felix Wohlrab_  
**15:50-16:10****Rheumatoid Arthritis |** A proteomic signature predicts flare and sustained drug-free remission in seropositive rheumatoid arthritis,_Jasmine Sim_  
**16:10-16:30****Expert Panel Discussion & Audience Q&A | **A moderated discussion exploring common biological pathways, emerging biomarker opportunities, and future directions for IMID research.

# Identification of novel blood-based signatures of neurodegenerative disease using high-sensitivity NULISA protein assays
Online
###### Topic:
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://www.labroots.com/virtual-event/neuroscience-2025?srsltid=AfmBOoq-TZJsX1O36mtQFrmnrdqy_kjHvI5KBnRqkqlmGl2Bewkgu_Qg)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Neuro-2025-1080x1080-1.png)
### Speaker
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Maura_Malpetti_100px.jpg)
Maura Malpetti, PhD
UK DRI Emerging Leader
Race Against Dementia ARUK Fellow Senior Research Associate University of Cambridge
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/SterlingJohnson2-300x300.jpg)
Sterling Johnson, PhD
Professor of Geriatrics and Dementia
Department of Geriatrics and Gerontology, University of Wisconsin


Join us for an insightful webinar exploring cutting-edge advancements in blood-based biomarker research for neurodegenerative diseases. Dr. Maura Malpetti and Dr. Sterling Johnson will present novel findings leveraging Alamar Biosciences’ highly sensitive NULISA™ immunoassay technology. This session will cover how multiplex proteomic analysis is unlocking new insights into Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and other neurodegenerative disorders, providing crucial data for early detection, differential diagnosis, and disease monitoring. The discussion will highlight Cambridge-based cohorts as well as the Wisconsin Registry for Alzheimer’s Prevention (WRAP) study, showcasing how blood biomarkers, including pTau, NfL, and inflammation markers, are reshaping our understanding of AD progression, multi-etiology dementia, and survival prediction.
Dr. Malpetti will discuss the role of inflammation and neurodegeneration in diseases beyond AD, including frontotemporal dementia (FTD) and progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP). Meanwhile, Dr. Johnson will delve into the challenges of identifying mixed-pathology dementia and how emerging biomarker tools enhance precision medicine approaches. Attendees will gain insights into the translational impact of large-scale proteomic screening, the integration of blood-based markers with imaging modalities, and the future of biomarker-driven clinical trials. Additionally, Doug Hinerfeld, Sr. Director of Field Application Support, will provide an overview of Alamar’s innovative NULISA technology and its role in accelerating discoveries in neurodegenerative research.
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://www.labroots.com/virtual-event/neuroscience-2025?srsltid=AfmBOoq-TZJsX1O36mtQFrmnrdqy_kjHvI5KBnRqkqlmGl2Bewkgu_Qg)

# Identifying blood-based signatures of Traumatic Brain Injury using high sensitivity, multiplexed protein assays
May 16, 2025
8:00 am PT / 11:00 am ET / 4:00 pm BST
###### Topic:
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://www.labroots.com/ms/webinar/identifying-blood-based-signatures-traumatic-brain-injury-using-sensitivity-multiplexed-protein-assa?utm_source=ucsf)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/David-Sharp-Imperial.jpg)
### Speaker
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Cheryl-wellington-thumbnail.jpg)
Cheryl Wellington, PhD
Professor and Vice Chair Research
Djavad Mowafaghian Centre for Brain Health Pathology and Laboratory Medicine The University of British Columbia
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/David-Sharp-Imperial.jpg)
Prof. David Sharp, PhD
UK Dementia Research Insitute and the Lead for the UK DRI Care Research and Technology Centre
Imperial College London


## Summary
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Scholarship_Featured_Labroots-768x768-1.png)Join Alamar Biosciences for an expert-led webinar exploring how emerging proteomics technologies—like [**NULISAseq™**](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/nulisa-assays-for-neurology/) high-sensitivity, multiplexed assays—are enabling more precise, scalable, and non-invasive tools to diagnose, stratify, and monitor traumatic brain injury (TBI), paving the way for improved patient care and therapeutic development.
Dr. David Sharp (Imperial College London) will present insights from his recent publication in Nature Medicine, which identifies distinct proteomic signatures of TBI. Dr. Cheryl Wellington (University of British Columbia) will share her translational research experience applying biomarker discovery approaches across both human and mouse models, highlighting the role of blood-based assays in bridging preclinical and clinical studies.
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://www.labroots.com/ms/webinar/identifying-blood-based-signatures-traumatic-brain-injury-using-sensitivity-multiplexed-protein-assa?utm_source=ucsf)
###### FOR RESEARCH USE ONLY. Not for use in diagnostic procedures.

# Identifying Predictive Biomarkers of Immune-related Adverse Events using High-Sensitivity Multiplexed NULISAseq Protein Assays​
Online
###### Topic:
###### Oncology
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://www.labroots.com/webinar/panel-presentation-identifying-non-invasive-predictive-biomarkers-immune-related-adverse-events-usin)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/virtual_event_header_banner_image_a3dfa34f5982f963f253535f3135acefa9972455_1317.png)
### Speaker
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/JamieLin.jpg)
Jamie S. Lin, MD
Assistant Professor​
Section of Nephrology The University of Texas, MD Anderson Cancer Center
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/NiyatiJhaveri.jpg)
Niyati Jhaveri, PhD​
Manager, Technology Access Program
Alamar Biosciences


## Summary
Join experts from MD Anderson Cancer Center and Alamar Biosciences as they present new research on predictive biomarkers of immune-related adverse events (irAEs) using advanced [NULISAseq™](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/nulisa-assays-for-immunology/) proteomic technology.
This session will feature Dr. Niyati Jhaveri, Manager of the Technology Access Program at Alamar Biosciences, presenting recent data from a longitudinal CAR-T toxicity study conducted in collaboration with Cleveland Clinic through Alamar’s Technology Access Program (TAP). Her talk will highlight how high-sensitivity NULISAseq™ assays reveal temporal patterns of biomarker responses mediating CAR-T-associated toxicities.
Dr. Jamie Lin, Assistant Professor, Section of Nephrology at MD Anderson Cancer Center, will follow with findings from a study leveraging [NULISA](https://alamarbio.com/technology/nulisa-platform/) technology to identify a non-invasive urine proteomic signature for diagnosing ICI-associated nephritis.
Gain insight into cutting-edge biomarker research in immuno-oncology, and see how high-sensitivity proteomics is advancing early, non-invasive, and precise prediction of immune-related toxicities. Register today!
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://www.labroots.com/webinar/panel-presentation-identifying-non-invasive-predictive-biomarkers-immune-related-adverse-events-usin)

# Inflammatory Protein Signatures Associated with Proneness to Early Life Infection and Asthma
Online
###### Topic:
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://event.on24.com/wcc/r/4190406/ACBADF15B23102E702657D2871E49855)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/genome-web-logo2.png)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/JessicaLaskySu.png)
### Presenters
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/JessicaLaskySu-300x300.png)
Jessica Lasky-Su, DSc, MS
Associate Professor in Medicine and Associate Statistician
Harvard Medical School and Brigham and Women’s Hospital
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/AlexForrestHay_crop2.png-300x300.jpg)
Alex Forrest-Hay
VP of Sales
Alamar Biosciences


## Summary
Immune development in early life is critical for establishing a trajectory toward long-term health; however, little is understood about how early-life inflammation may impact immune development.
In this webinar, **Jessica Lasky-Su** , associate professor in medicine at Harvard Medical School and Brigham and Women’s Hospital, will discuss a study in which she and colleagues measured 203 inflammatory protein targets across 180 samples from healthy children at ages 1 and 6 using Alamar Biosciences’ NULISAseq Inflammation panel. The team identified the inflammatory proteins at age 1 that were associated with proneness to infection and the development of asthma by age 6. They also characterized critical changes in the inflammatory profile that developed among those with infection proneness and asthma by age 6. Finally, they assessed the impact of sex on these findings.

# Neurodegenerative Disease Biomarker Detection Using an Ultra-Sensitive Profiling Method
Online
###### Topic:
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://www.workcast.cohttps//www.workcast.com/register?cpak=3018982020663234)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/GENlogo_ColorBackground_062618_200.png)
### Speaker
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/HenrikZetterbergHS-300x300.png)
Henrik Zetterberg, MD, PhD
Professor of Neurochemistry
University of Gothenburg
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/DougHinerfeld-300x300.png)
Doug Hinerfeld, PhD
Senior Director of Application Support
Alamar Biosciences


Brain-derived biomarkers of neurodegenerative diseases are important targets for new therapies. In the context of Alzheimer’s disease, scientists are exploring the use of protein biomarkers for early diagnosis, screening, prognosis prediction, and disease monitoring. But these markers are often present at very low concentrations in plasma or serum, much too low for most existing proteomics assays to detect and measure.
In this GEN webinar, Henrik Zetterberg, MD, PhD, an expert in Alzheimer’s disease, will discuss his efforts to discover and validate blood-based biomarkers for various CNS disorders. During his presentation, he will share data from his evaluation of the NULISA immunoassay platform’s ability to detect biomarkers of Alzheimer’s disease from serum. You will also hear from Doug Hinerfeld, PhD, who will discuss the NULISA platform’s multiplex and protein marker detection capabilities in more depth.
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://www.workcast.cohttps//www.workcast.com/register?cpak=3018982020663234)

# NULISA : la précision de la protéomique ultrasensible et multiplexée au service du diagnostic précoce
November 25, 2025
Online
###### Topic:
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_CQzO1cYoSWO8V_QF_NeCsw)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/1080x1080-data.png)
### Speaker
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/HS-Amelie-Castro-300x300.png)
Amélie Castro
Snr. Regional Business Manager, BeNeLux
Alamar Biosciences


##### **Disponible en replay**
[**NULISA ™**](https://alamarbio.com/technology/nulisa-platform/) est une nouvelle technologie de protéomique**ultrasensible et multiplexée** , conçue pour détecter les protéines à des niveaux extrêmement bas, impossibles à mesurer jusqu’ici. Grâce à sa**grande précision** et à sa capacité à analyser de nombreux biomarqueurs simultanément, NULISA ouvre la voie à une **médecine de précision** plus efficace.
Son objectif : permettre la **détection très précoce** de nombreuses maladies, bien avant l’apparition des symptômes, afin d’améliorer la prévention, le diagnostic et le suivi des patients.
#### AGENDA
  * Présentation de la technologie
  * Présentation des panels disponibles
  * Bénéfices pour les maladies neurodégénératives
  * Bénéfices pour les maladies Inflammatoires et auto-immunes.
  * Aspects pratiques : où et comment accéder à NULISA
  * Q&A


[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_CQzO1cYoSWO8V_QF_NeCsw)
###### FOR RESEARCH USE ONLY. Not for use in diagnostic procedures.

# NULISA : protéomique ultrasensible et multiplexée au service de l’immunologie et des maladies infectieuses
July 1, 2026
Zoom Webinar
2:00 pm CEST
###### Topic:
###### Immunology
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_E04xWygvSNal7iznVU5CHg)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/immune-cell.gif)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/immune-cell.gif)
### Speaker
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/HS-Amelie-Castro-300x300.png)
Amélie Castro
Snr. Regional Business Manager, France & BeNeLux
Alamar Biosciences
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/HS-Veronique-Berchet-300x300.png)
Veronique Berchet
Field Application Scientist
Alamar Biosciences


## Summary
**NULISA™** est une technologie de protéomique **ultrasensible et multiplexée** , capable de détecter des protéines à des concentrations extrêmement faibles — bien en dessous des limites des technologies conventionnelles. Grâce à sa **précision inégalée** et à sa capacité à mesurer des centaines de biomarqueurs simultanément à partir d’un volume minimal d’échantillon, NULISA représente une avancée majeure pour la recherche en immunologie et en maladies infectieuses.
Ce webinaire est organisé en partenariat avec la **SFR Biosciences** (Lyon), qui fédère de nombreuses équipes de recherche et met a disposition des plateformes technologiques de haut niveau en sciences du vivant, afin de soutenir l’innovation et les collaborations scientifiques.
Découvrez comment NULISA peut transformer vos recherches : du profilage cytokinique à haute résolution à la caractérisation fine des réponses immunitaires, jusqu’à l’identification de nouveaux biomarqueurs d’infection et d’inflammation.
Au Programme
  * Présentation de la technologie NULISA
  * Présentation des panels disponibles ([NULISAseq™ Inflammation Panel 250 & Panel AQ](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/nulisa-assays-for-immunology/))
  * Cas 1: profilage immunitaire ultra-sensible pour la détection de protéines inflammatoires chez les patients COVID-19
  * Cas 2 : identification de cytokines corrélées à une augmentation des réponses en anticorps dans le cadre d’études sur la vaccination contre la grippe
  * Cas 3 : Leucémie Aiguë Myéloïde: profilage du protéome et identification de nouveaux biomarqueurs inflammatoires permettant d’améliorer les modèles de stratification classiques
  * Q&A


[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_E04xWygvSNal7iznVU5CHg)

# Ultra‑Sensitive Proteomics for Neurodegeneration: NULISA™ / ARGO™ HT Launch at Amsterdam UMC – On Demand
May 21, 2026
Recorded May 21, 2026
###### Topic:
###### Neurology
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://vimeo.com/showcase/12271402?fl=so&fe=fs)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/AUMC-logo.png)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/AUMC-logo.png)
### Speaker
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/HS-Charlotte-Teunissen-300x300.png)
Prof. Charlotte Teunissen
Professor in Neurochemistry
Amsterdam UMC
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/HS_Mathias-Holpert-300x300.png)
Mathias Holpert
Manager, EMEA Field Application Scientist
Alamar Biosciences
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Hs-G-Salvado-300x300.png)
Dr. Gemma Salvadó
Group Leader of the Neuroimaging Research Group at BBRC
Barcelona Beta & Lund University
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/HS-Monique-Bretler-300x300.png)
Prof. Monique Breteler
Director of Population Health Sciences
DZNE
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/HS-J-Rohrer-300x300.png)
Prof. Jonathan Rohrer
Professor of Neurology
UCL
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/HS-S-Kezic-300x300.png)
Dr. Sanja Kezic
Senior Principal Scientist
Amsterdam UMC
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/HS-Amy-Fu-300x300.png)
Prof. Amy Fu
Associate Professor
Hong Kong University of Science and Technology


## Summary
The Grand Opening of the NULISA™ platform at Amsterdam UMC brought together an international group of researchers to explore advances in ultra‑sensitive proteomics and biomarker research. Five sessions from the scientific programme are now available to watch on demand.
Speakers include **Dr. Gemma Salvadó** (Barcelonaβeta & Lund University), and **Mathias Holpert** (Alamar Biosciences), covering applications across Alzheimer’s disease, frontotemporal dementia, dermatology, and an introduction to the NULISA™ platform itself.
Select any session to get started. Where recordings are not available, talk summaries are shown.
**Programme**
**Session 1 |****Introduction to NULISA technology: A new ultra-highly sensitive proteomics platform for profiling low abundant fluid-based biomarker,**_Mathias Holpert, Alamar Biosciences_
**Session 2 |****Plasma and CSF proteomic signatures related to Alzheimer’s, α synuclein, or vascular pathologies and clinical decline,**_Dr. Gemma Salvadó, Barcelona Beta & Lund University_
**Session 3**** | Proteomics profiling of healthy and unhealthy brain ageing in the Rhineland study, **_Prof. Monique Breteler, DZNE. Session overview available – recording not currently available._
**Session 4 |****NULISA analysis in genetic frontotemporal dementia: a study on the GENetic FTD Initiative** , _Prof. Jonathan Rohrer, UCL. Session overview available – recording not currently available._
**Session 5 |****Stratum Corneum Biomarkers in Dermatological Research: Potential and Methodological Challenge,**_Dr. Sanja Kezic, Amsterdam UMC. Session overview available – recording not currently available._
**Session 6 |****Blood Proteomic Analysis Using Ultra-sensitive Assays: Insights for the Accurate Classification and Staging of Alzheimer’s Disease Pathology,** Prof. Amy Fu, Hong Kong University of Science and Technology. _Session overview available – recording not currently available._
**Session 7 |****KEY LECTURE ‘The Amsterdam experience: reliable measurement of biomarkers for dementias and multiple sclerosis using NULISA’,**_Prof. Charlotte Teunissen, Amsterdam UMC. Session overview available – recording not currently available._

# Unraveling Ankylosing Spondylitis: Integrating Proteomics with Global Genetic Meta-Analysis
November 11, 2025
Online
8:00 am PT / 11:00 am ET / 4:00 pm GMT
###### Topic:
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://www.genengnews.com/multimedia/webinars/unraveling-ankylosing-spondylitis-integrating-proteomics-with-global-genetic-meta-analysis/?utm_source=webpage)
### Presenters
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Headshot-outline.jpg)
Nicholas Harvey, PhD
Postdoctoral Research Associate King’s College London


## Summary
Ankylosing Spondylitis (AS) is a debilitating, immune-mediated disease which causes inflammation of the joints between the vertebrae, leading to stiffness, pain, and eventually fusion of the spine. The underpinnings of AS are highly complex and span genetic, environmental, and immunologic factors. Insights from proteomic analysis helps with mapping risk factors and identifying potential therapeutic targets.
In this GEN webinar, our expert speaker, Nicholas Harvey, PhD, will present findings from the largest genome-wide association study (GWAS) meta-analysis of AS to date, integrating data across diverse ancestries (e.g. European, East Asian, Turkish, and Iranian) and multiple omic layers, including the transcriptome, proteome, Mendelian randomization, and microbiome. During the webinar, you will gain new insights into AS pathogenesis, therapeutic challenges, and novel avenues for precision medicine.
**Key takeaways:**
  * The identification of novel AS loci and signals, including 27 new genome-wide significant loci and 86 independent non-MHC associations
  * The connection between AS risk and secretor status in the gut microbiome
  * The impact of longer leukocyte telomeres on AS susceptibility
  * The role of cytokine biology in therapy efficacy
  * How to prioritize genes by applying fine-mapping to highlight causal variants


[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://www.genengnews.com/multimedia/webinars/unraveling-ankylosing-spondylitis-integrating-proteomics-with-global-genetic-meta-analysis/?utm_source=webpage)

# Utilizing NULISA, A Novel Ultrasensitive Multiplex Proteomic Panel for Comprehensive Neurological Disease Profiling including ALS/MND
September 16, 2026
11:00 am – 12:00 pm Australia/Melbourne
###### Topic:
###### Neurology
[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_vMlyZMwJQmCWsVLLA6oOCg)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/AlamarBiosciencesInc-329942-Treating-Neurological-Disorders-blogbanner2.jpg)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Australia-ALS-26.png)
### Speaker
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Image-2-1-e1782269507757-300x300.jpg)
Caroline Chan, PhD
Distributor Application Scientist Manager
Alamar Biosciences
  * ![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Kat_Stracke-e1787898846525-300x300.jpg)
Katharina Stracke, PhD
Technical Sales Representative - Proteomics
Geneworks


## Summary
With comprehensive coverage of the hallmarks of neurological disease, the NULISAseq™ Neuro 220 Panel offers unprecedented insight into the biological mechanisms involved in Alzheimer’s Disease, Parkinson’s Disease, Traumatic Brain Injury, Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis/Motor neuron disease (MND), Multiple Sclerosis and Gliomas.
Join us for a webinar to discover how the Neuro 220 panel enables researchers to detect co-pathologies and disease heterogeneity with precision.
**At the end of the webinar, find out how you can apply for the Neuro 220 pilot program for researchers in Australia and New Zealand to advance your biomarker studies.**
**Case study spotlight at the webinar**
  * Motor neuron disease (MND), including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), remains one of the most devastating neurodegenerative disorders, marked by clinical heterogeneity, delayed diagnosis, and limited therapeutic success. A central barrier to progress has been the lack of accessible, reliable targets that capture disease biology while enabling early diagnosis and monitoring.
  * We will showcase how new precision proteomic technologies such as NULISA have transformed our ability to study ALS/MND through accessible patient biospecimens such as blood and CSF and accelerated the discovery of blood-based biomarkers associated with disease diagnosis, progression, and biological heterogeneity.


[ VIEW ON DEMAND ](https://zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_vMlyZMwJQmCWsVLLA6oOCg)
###### FOR RESEARCH USE ONLY. Not for use in diagnostic procedures.

# Alamar Precision Proteomics Summit, Rochester, MN (Hybrid)
October 30, 2026
Rochester, MN, United States
9:00 am – 12:00 pm CT
###### Topic:
###### Booth:
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/APPS-Mayo-clinic-0623-1-1.jpg)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/APPS-Mayo-clinic-0623-1-1.jpg)
## Event Details
#### IN PERSON  
Rochester Marriott Mayo Clinic Area  
Ballroom (2nd floor)  
101 1st Ave SW, Rochester, MN 55902
VIRTUAL  
Mayo Clinic – Arizona (7:00 am – 10:00 am PT)  
Mayo Clinic – Jacksonville (10:00 am – 1:00 pm ET)
#### Unlock the Power of Fluid Biomarkers
Join Alamar Biosciences and Key Opinion Leaders from Mayo Clinic, University of Minnesota, University of Chicago, and Alamar Biosciences for a hybrid scientific event exploring the latest advances in protein biomarker research and an introduction to NULISA™, a precision proteomics platform delivering ultra-high sensitivity and high multiplex protein detection from blood.
The main event will take place live in Rochester, MN and will be broadcast virtually to Mayo Clinic Arizona and Jacksonville, bringing together scientists and researchers across the broader Mayo community for a collaborative discussion on emerging biomarker technologies and applications.
Learn how researchers are utilizing the [**NULISA™ Platform**](https://alamarbio.com/technology/nulisa-platform/) and [**ARGO™ HT System** ](https://alamarbio.com/products-and-services/argo-system/)to accelerate protein biomarker discovery and translational research. This event is open to all scientists and researchers across the Mayo Clinic community.

## AAIC 2026 – Novel Plasma Biomarkers Associated with Amyloid PET Positivity and Tau PET Staging across the Alzheimer’s Disease Continuum
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/CUK-Poster_AAIC-2026-300x300.png)
  * July 15, 2026
  * Xiao-Jun Ma, et al.


###### Product:
######  Alzheimer's, Neurology
###### Topic:
###### Disease Area:
###### Alzheimer's Disease
###### Sample Type:
###### Plasma
Back to Publications​ 
  * July 15, 2026


###### Topic/Product:
######  Alzheimer's, Neurology
###### Disease Area:
###### Alzheimer's Disease
###### Sample Type:
###### Plasma
## Study Objective and Cohort
**Background** : Blood-based biomarkers (BBMs) are transforming Alzheimer’s disease (AD) diagnosis and staging. While pTau-217 emerging as the lead BBM for identifying AD pathology, additional biomarkers are needed to fully implement diagnostic and staging frameworks. Here, we employed ultrasensitive NULISA (Nucleic acid-Linked Immuno-Sandwich Assay)1 technology to analyze a well-characterized Korean cohort to identify novel proteins along the AD progression continuum.
**Methods:** We developed the NULISAseq Neuro 220 Panel for the detection of >220 biomarkers associated with neuroinflammation, synaptic pathology, and vascular dysfunction including brain-derived (BD) pTaus and eMTBR Tau. We analyzed 300 plasma samples (mean age = 75.42, 71.33% females) from cognitively unimpaired individuals (CU, n=93), mild cognitive impairment (MCI, n=163) and dementia cases (n=44) and used linear regression models to identify differentially expressed (DE) proteins and those associated with amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) positivity (centiloid _> _20) and ATN PET staging.

## High-plex Proteomic Characterization of Pre-clinical models with the NULSAseq Mouse Panel 120
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/ADPD-2025_Mouse-Poster-233x300.png)

Back to Publications​

######  mouse, Neurology
###### Disease Area:
###### Sample Type:
## Abstract
**Objectives:** With the emergence of several preclinical models of neurodegenerative diseases including Alzheimer’s Disease (AD), proteomic characterization of these models is needed to better understand their clinical relevance and utility in therapeutic evaluation. Along with amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles, neuroinflammation is an underlying mechanism of disease progression and a multiplex proteomics approach is needed to track the temporal regulation of inflammatory and neurodegenerative processes as well as the degree to which these preclinical models recapitulate the biology of the human disease. 
**Methods:** Previously, we developed a 250-plex Inflammation Panel and 120-plex CNS Disease Panel on the automated ARGO platform to profile key proteins such as IL6, phospho-Tau, and amyloid beta for profiling of biofluids in human studies. To provide a complementary approach for proteomic profiling in preclinical models, we have developed a 120-plex Mouse Panel for detection of cytokines, growth factors and other CNS disease targets. Plasma samples from different mouse strains were assayed at multiple input volumes. CSF and brain lysates were also evaluated. Dilutional linearity, reproducibility and overall detectability were assessed. Additionally, various preclinical models of AD and Traumatic Brain Injury were also evaluated. 
**Results:** Our results demonstrate robust performance with 5% median intra-assay CV and 97.4% detectability in mouse plasma samples from 5 common strains. Additionally, lowering sample input volume from 10uL to 5uL has minimal impact on overall detectability (>95%), reflecting high assay sensitivity. Dilutional linearity further demonstrated good target linearity with signal-to-noise ratio over 2 for 97% of the targets in the panel. The analytical validation along with the application of the panel across different AD models demonstrates the utility of the multiplex NULISAseq™ Mouse Panel for comprehensive characterization of neurodegenerative and inflammatory markers in preclinical models.

## Proteome Profiling of Dried Blood Spots and Plasma Spots with NULISAseq™ Inflammation and CNS Disease Panels

## Abstract
**Purpose:** Population-wide profiling of blood-based biomarkers is important for early detection of diseases and risk assessments to ease the increasing global healthcare burden. Reliable testing requires standardized sampling, collection and storage methods particularly in remote areas with low infrastructure. With the availability of metered collection devices, dried blood spots (DBS) and dried plasma spots (DPS) have emerged as an alternative source for cross sectional and longitudinal studies across large cohorts. Due to the limited amount of sample material in DBS and DPS, proteomic analysis demands highly sensitive and multiplexed platforms for comprehensive profiling to detect key biomarkers of inflammation, neurodegeneration and disease pathology.
**Methods:** The NULISA Inflammation Panel 250 and CNS Disease Panel 120 were deployed to compare proteomic profiles in DBS and DPS with matched whole blood and plasma from healthy and diseased individuals. Multiple parameters such as collection devices, extraction conditions and input volumes were tested to identify optimal protocols for detection of key biomarkers on the ARGO HT platform. Correlation analysis was performed to determine concordance with paired whole blood and plasma.
**Results:** Preliminary data reveal high detectability for key markers such as NFL, GFAP and pTaus in DBS and DPS. Overall detectability across the panels for DBS and DPS (>85%) is comparable with detectability of proteins Overall detectability across the panels for DBS and DPS (>85%) is comparable with detectability of proteins in whole blood and plasma. Additionally, Pearson correlation analyses show high concordance in relative quantification of most proteins between matched DBS/blood and DPS/plasma samples.
**Conclusion:** Our data demonstrate the potential of DBS/DPS as a promising alternative for blood-based profiling with ease of collection, storage and transportation for large scale studies. The low volume requirements coupled with the high throughput automation offered with ARGO make it an ideal platform for multiplexed proteomic analysis of this unique sample type with a wide range of applications in global screening and risk profiling studies.

###### Sample Type:
## Abstract
**Purpose:** Aging is associated with an increased susceptibility to cancer and many chronic autoimmune, neurodegenerative, and metabolic diseases. Characterizing the underlying mechanisms regulating the development and progression of these conditions demands a highly sensitive, non-invasive and multiplexed approach to study age-related proteomic changes.
**Methods:** We recently developed a high throughput and automated immunoassay platform, Nucleic-acid linked immunosandwich assay (NULISA), capable of detecting 100s of proteins simultaneously with attomolar sensitivity. NULISA combines a novel background suppression approach with the specificity of proximity ligation to achieve high sensitivity and wide dynamic range. Using two targeted panels, the NULISAseq 250-plex Inflammation Panel and 120-plex CNS Disease Panel, encompassing a broad range of cytokines, chemokines and key neurodegeneration-related proteins (pTau, β-amyloid proteins, synucleins), on the ARGO HT™ platform, we sought to profile plasma samples from a curated clinical cohort of >500 male and female subjects spanning over 7 decades of chronological age with diverse racial/ethnic backgrounds.
**Results:** The NULISAseq Inflammation and CNS Disease Panels demonstrated 98.9% and 96.8% target detectability in the plasma cohort, respectively. Linear model analysis by age and sex further revealed differential abundance with age of >250 targets including proinflammatory cytokines such as TNFα, TGFβ and IL6 and CNS markers like pTau-217, pTau-181, pTau-231 and amyloid beta proteins (38, 40 and 42). In addition, GDNF, CRH, FCN2, FLT1, IL24 and CXCL12 showed age-dependent downregulation. Further analyses with elastic net models demonstrated that <200 age-related proteins could accurately predict chronological age. Protein interaction analysis of these biomarker signatures revealed an intricate network of interconnected cytokines, consistent with inflammaging.
**Conclusion:** In summary, the high-plex NULISAseq dataset generated from analysis of >300 proteins in a large cohort of individuals with a broad age distribution provides a valuable resource to study changes in inflammation and neurodegeneration-related proteins with age and their association with age-related clinical outcomes.

## Background
Risk stratification in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is critical to tailor timely induction therapy. The most widely utilized risk stratification approach is the European LeukemiaNet (ELN) that usually requires bone marrow biopsy and genomic testing. Inflammation is increasingly recognized as a critical factor in AML. Novel biomarkers from robust blood-based tests are needed to accurately and efficiently risk stratify patients with newly diagnosed AML.
## Methods
— Inflammatory proteome was evaluated through blood-based proteomic profiling of 251 soluble inflammatory proteins using NUcleic acid Linked Immuno-Sandwich Assay (NULISA), a proximity-ligation assay based on NGS or PCR allowing attomolar (10-18) detection in 543 newly diagnosed AML patients   
— Multivariable cox models with L1 regularization were used to test the independent  
prognostic ability. A seven-protein prognostic score (Leukemia Inflammatory Risk Score, LIRS) was developed   
— Model performance was assessed by cumulative concordance index (C-index) and time-dependent area under the curve (tdAUC).  
— Findings were validated in internal and external cohorts, including a prospective cohort of newly diagnosed AML patients.

## Comprehensive Characterization of Inflammatory Cytokines in Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia Highlight Immune Dysregulation and Associates with MRD
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Poster_MDA_ASH2024-2-300x187.png)

###### Oncology
###### Disease Area:
###### Sample Type:
## Background
Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) is characterized by immune dysfunction and dysregulation resulting in increased risk for infection and second cancers. Prior studies indicated that chronic inflammation may contribute to worse clinical course in CLL. Comprehensive assessment of the inflammatory mediators and in context of response to treatment, particularly measurable residual disease (MRD), remains unexplored. We aimed to leverage a novel proteomic profiling of >250 inflammatory proteins with high sensitivity assay to assess serum inflammatory profiles at baseline and post-treatment and associations with MRD status.
## Sample and Methods
— Baseline samples of 64 CLL patients treated first-line therapy on the randomized trial of acalabrutinib (ACA) + venetoclax (VEN) +/- early obinutuzumab (OBIN) (NCT04169737)  
— 18 patients with a paired end of treatment (EOC26) sample with bone marrow (BM) undetectable MRD status (uMRD4; 10-4 sensitivity)  
— 26 healthy donor plasma samples as control  
— Inflammatory proteome was evaluated through blood-based proteomic profiling of 251 soluble inflammatory proteins using NUcleic acid Linked Immuno-Sandwich Assay (NULISA), a proximity-ligation assay based on NGS or PCR allowing attomolar (10-18) detection  
— Comparative analysis to identify differentially expressed cytokines at baseline or EOC26 compared to healthy to define dysregulated inflammatory protein networks  
— Logistic regression to assess cytokines prognostic for early uMRD4 at EOC9

## Ultrasensitive profiling of >300 plasma proteins for predicting biological age (HUPO 2024 & BoAC 2024)
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/HUPO-2024_Aging-Poster_Final_print-223x300.png)

###### Disease Area:

## Abstract
Biological aging underlies almost all major chronic diseases such as cancer, autoimmune diseases and Alzheimer’s disease. Elucidating the biological mechanisms of aging and monitoring the aging process noninvasively holds great promise for the early detection and ultimately the prevention of aging-related diseases. Current approaches to quantify biological age have mostly focused on epigenetic changes in the genome. Advances in proteomic technologies can provide an alternative and arguably more actionable measure of biological aging at the protein level. Here we apply the recently developed Nucleic acid-linked immunosandwich assay (NULISA)_1_ to measure >300 proteins to assess age-related changes in plasma protein levels. 
In this study, we profiled a cohort of 500 individuals spanning over 7 decades of chronological age from a biobank maintained by a major metropolitan academic medical center. The cohort consisted of an even balance of male and female subjects and is generally representative of the racial/ethnic distribution of the collection site. Plasma samples from this cohort were assayed with the NULISAseq 250-plex Inflammation and 120-plex CNS Disease Panels targeting key inflammation-related cytokines and chemokines and proteins involved in all major hallmarks of neurodegeneration such as pTau and β-amyloid proteins.
Overall target detectability in plasma samples from this cohort was 98.8% with the Inflammation Panel and 96.8% with the CNS Disease Panel. Preliminary bioinformatics analyses identified >150 targets from the Inflammation Panel that were increased with age including proinflammatory markers such as IL6, TNFα, LIF, TGFβ and IL18. Analysis with the CNS markers further identified age-dependent increases in pTau-217, pTau-181, pTau-231, Aβs (38, 40 and 42) as well as NEFL and NEFH among many other markers implicated in neurodegeneration. Additional analyses are planned to build a protein-based age predictor and assess its correlation with clinical outcomes to predict mortality and common diseases.
In conclusion, this study applied the recently developed NULISA platform to profile key inflammation and neurodegeneration-related proteins in plasma in a well curated clinical cohort. The large number of proteins identified to be associated with age indicates that this dataset may provide a rich and high-quality dataset for the aging research community.

## HUPO 2024 Poster: Development of NULISAseq™ Inflammation Panel 250 for Comprehensive Immune Profiling
![](https://alamarbio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/NULISAseq-IF-Panel-250_FOCIS-2024-Poster_Print-223x300.png)
